title: Design Engineer
description:
Since early 2024, we've gone from 0 to over 900 customers, succeeding where many have tried and failed before. We have a big mission: to make it wildly easier and more profitable to run and grow a renewables installation business, and through that to make a real dent in the world's carbon emissions and a far better experience for homeowners.

We're now looking for a Design Engineer who wants to design & ship exceptional outcomes for users. Most of our product is a front end over hard physics (heat-loss calculations, hydronic design, LiDAR floor plans, compliance that has to be right), used by installers on a phone, with no signal, in a hurry. Making that feel simple is a design problem and an engineering problem at the same time, and this role sits right on that seam.

🌲 About Spruce

- Almost 20% of the UK's carbon emissions comes from heating homes – there's simply no way to reach net zero without phasing out gas and oil boilers. Right now the only serious alternative is heat pumps, with their almost-magical ability to turn 1 kW of electricity into 3-5 kW of heat (🤯). But the heat pump installation journey is slow, inefficient, and just so painful. This makes it hard for existing installers to grow their businesses and puts off gas engineers from starting to do heat pumps. Perhaps most critically, it means you can't currently offer a heat pump when someone's boiler breaks and they urgently need heating.

- We're fixing this. We've built a platform for heat pump installers to manage the whole installation journey from initial enquiry through to final compliance paperwork, freeing up their time to focus on what really matters: doing high-quality installations, providing great customer service, and scaling their business. Despite only getting started at the beginning of 2024, we're having a massive impact on installation businesses, suppliers, and manufacturers across the UK: halving the time they spend on each job and doubling their sales conversion rates.

- We raised a chunky Seed round last year from top-tier investors and this year have grown the team 3x and revenue 4x. We've expanded into Ireland, are launching an end-to-end solar and battery product in November, and are increasingly becoming the operating system for the whole home renewables supply chain. If you can picture a combination of ServiceTitan, Procore, and AutoCAD, you might get a sense of where we're headed…

🥖 The role

You'll own how the product looks, feels and behaves wherever installers use it, from the first sketch to the shipped feature. Installers only adopt Spruce if it's easy to use on a real job, and adoption is what drives our growth. That puts your work at the centre of the business. Day-to-day you'll be:

- Designing and shipping – You'll take a flow from rough idea all the way to production, prototyping in whatever gets you to an answer fastest (often code, sometimes Figma or a sketch), and testing with installers as you go. The gap between "we should fix this" and "it's fixed" is often a day.

- Owning the interaction layer – You'll build and look after the component library and the patterns underneath it: motion, loading and empty states, touch targets that still work with gloves on. The small things that make a complex tool feel simple.

- Building the parts that are hard to get right – The canvas-based floor plan and system design tools, the offline survey app (incl. LiDAR), the proposals homeowners see. These are the parts where the UI is the product, and where we've got the most still to build.

- Raising the bar on everything we ship – You'll work closely with our product designers and developers, pairing on their work and reviewing it, so the quality of what you build rubs off on the rest of the product.

- Spending time with installers – You'll go out on site, watch how the product actually gets used, then come back and change it.

You'll report to Steph , our co-founder and CPO (she’s pretty awesome) and you’ll work alongside Dan & Arron who’ve cooked up some incredible work in their time so far.

🫵 About you

We look for the same five things in everyone at Spruce: curiosity; intense drive, ambition and work ethic; a high degree of personal agency and ownership; deep humility and a growth mindset; and excellent craft. You might currently call yourself a designer who ships, a front-end engineer with strong design instincts, or already a design engineer. We're looking for 3+ years of experience (and potentially a lot more) designing and building product UI, ideally in a startup or a fast-paced, impact-focussed team. We'd love to speak with you if you have:

- Real taste, and shipped work to prove it – You can show us production UI you designed and built, and talk about why the details are the way they are. Work you'd happily put next to the best-crafted B2B products out there.

- Strong design craft, and a real appetite for code – You're a strong designer first. You don't need to be a front-end engineer, and you might well ship with Cursor or Claude Code, but you want to understand the code you're shipping. Bonus for React and TypeScript depth, canvas/WebGL, animation, or complex state on mobile.

- A prototyping instinct – You'd rather build a rough version and test it than argue about it in a doc. You're comfortable with things being imperfect in front of users.

- Systems thinking – You enjoy the structure of a good component library and understand that consistency is what lets a small team ship fast. You also know when to slow down first: you value time spent on lo-fi wireframes and on understanding the data model before anything gets polished.

- Curiosity about the domain – You want to understand how heating systems, solar and battery actually work, and you pick up technical detail fast. By the end of week two you'll be arguing about the best way to show a homeowner their solar self-consumption.

🌟 Our offer

- 💰 £60-110k salary, depending on experience and location

- 🍰 Meaningful slice of equity (options) in the company

- 🏖️ 33 days holiday (25 plus bank holidays) and opportunity to work from abroad for another 30 days each year

- 🏡 Hybrid working: 2–3 days in-person a week (London or Bristol), with full-team meetups every fortnight

- 🏥 Private Medical Cover (Vitality)

- 👧 Workplace Nursery Benefit scheme ( YellowNest )

- 🧑‍🍼 Enhanced Parental Leave

- 🚲 Cycle to Work scheme

- 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Brilliant team to learn from and massive opportunity to grow

🧑‍💻 Working at Spruce

- We're currently a close-knit team of 34, split between London and Bristol. We spend 2-3 days each week working together in-person in both locations, and get everyone together every fortnight.

- You'll have genuine influence from day one. The best idea wins regardless of seniority. We expect you to challenge everything, ask "why?" multiple levels deep, and push back when something doesn't make sense.

- We want everyone to spend time with installers on-site, feel their pain points, then be able to rapidly suggest and implement solutions based on real feedback rather than assumptions. This is clearly particularly important for this role but you'll be surrounded by a whole team who are also close to our customers.

- We move fast and ship imperfect things, learning from users rather than trying to perfect in isolation. When things break, we focus on how we fix it, what we can learn, and never blame. You'll own your outcomes whilst knowing the team has your back.

- Feedback is constant, direct, and kind. We'll tell you when something isn't working and expect the same honesty (and empathy) back.

Compensation: £60K – £110K • Offers Equity

title: Senior Software Engineer, Backend (AI Agent Integrations)
description:
Cresta unlocks the true potential of the customer experience, turning every conversation into a competitive advantage. Cresta’s unified AI platform combines conversational AI agents, real-time human agent augmentation, and comprehensive conversation intelligence to drive revenue and efficiency gains across every channel. The world’s leading companies, including United Airlines, Cox Communications, and Marriott, use Cresta to power world-class customer experiences every day. 

Born from the Stanford AI Lab, Cresta has raised more than $270 million from the world’s leading investors, including a16z, Greylock, and Sequoia. Cresta’s leadership includes some of the leading minds in AI today. Our CEO, Ping Wu , founded and led Google's Contact Center AI and Vertex AI platforms before joining Cresta to build the future of AI-driven customer experiences.

Over the next few years, AI is going to redefine how people all over the world interact with businesses every day. Come build that future at Cresta.

About the role:

Cresta’s AI Agent team is building enterprise-grade AI Agents that can operate inside real-world contact center environments. A critical part of that mission is enabling our AI Agents to seamlessly integrate with customers’ CCaaS platforms (Contact Center as a Service), including voice and digital channels — and to smoothly transition conversations between AI and human agents when needed.

This role is focused on building the backend systems that allow our AI Agents to:

- Integrate deeply with leading CCaaS platforms

- Participate in live customer conversations across voice and chat

- Maintain full conversation state and context

- Perform real-time actions within the CCaaS ecosystem

- Seamlessly hand off conversations to human agents — without losing context, history, or workflow state

- Support human agents with AI assistance after transfer

We are looking for strong backend engineers who want to work at the intersection of distributed systems, real-time communication, enterprise integrations, and AI Agent orchestration.

This is not a pure research role — it is about building production-grade infrastructure that enables AI Agents to operate reliably in mission-critical customer environments.

Why This Role Is Unique: 

- AI + Real-Time Systems : Work on infrastructure that enables AI Agents to participate in live conversations at scale.

- Enterprise-Grade Integrations : Design robust integrations with major CCaaS platforms and customer systems.

- Human-AI Collaboration : Build the systems that make AI-to-human handoff seamless, contextual, and reliable.

- High-Impact Engineering : Your work directly determines how smoothly AI Agents operate in production environments.

If you’re a strong backend engineer who wants to apply your expertise to real-world AI systems operating inside complex enterprise ecosystems, this role offers that opportunity.

Responsibilities :

- Design and build scalable backend services that integrate Cresta’s AI Agents with customers’ CCaaS platforms.

- Architect systems that manage real-time conversation state, context propagation, and session lifecycle.

- Implement seamless AI-to-human handoff mechanisms, ensuring full context transfer and minimal disruption to the customer experience.

- Develop secure and reliable integrations with CCaaS APIs (voice, chat, messaging, routing, agent desktop, etc.).

- Collaborate closely with ML engineers and AI researchers to operationalize AI Agent capabilities in live environments.

- Ensure high availability, low latency, and strong observability for real-time conversation systems.

- Implement authentication, authorization, compliance, and enterprise security best practices across integrations.

- Drive improvements in reliability, performance, and scalability in production environments handling high interaction volumes

Qualifications We Value: 

- Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or related field.

- 5+ years of experience building scalable backend systems in production environments.

- Strong experience designing and maintaining robust APIs (REST, gRPC).

- Solid understanding of distributed systems and real-time communication architectures.

- Experience integrating with third-party enterprise platforms and APIs.

- Experience working with CCaaS platforms or contact center systems is a strong plus.

- Familiarity with AI Agents, Virtual Agents, or LLM-based systems is a plus.

- Experience with containerized environments (Kubernetes, Docker).

- Experience with cloud platforms such as AWS, GCP, or Azure.

- Strong understanding of system reliability, observability, and security in enterprise environments.

Perks & Benefits: 

- We offer Cresta employees a variety of medical, dental, and vision plans, designed to fit you and your family’s needs

- Paid parental leave to support you and your family

- Monthly Health & Wellness allowance

- Work from home office stipend to help you succeed in a remote environment

- Lunch reimbursement for in-office employees 

- PTO: 3 weeks in Canada 

Compensation for this position includes a base salary, equity, and a variety of benefits. Actual base salaries will be based on candidate-specific factors, including experience, skillset, and location, and local minimum pay requirements as applicable. We are actively hiring for this role in the US and Canada. Your recruiter can provide further details.

title: Senior Backend Engineer - Search Features & APIs (SABR)
description:
About us

Launched in 2019, Constructor is an AI-first e-commerce search and discovery platform that helps shoppers find the right products at the right time and enables leading global e-commerce brands to drive meaningful revenue and conversion gains.

About the team

The SABR team owns the top layer of request processing for product discovery. We own the service that first receives product discovery requests (autocomplete, search, browse & recommendations) & executes the entire business logic that drives product discovery. That service also functions as a gateway to parse incoming user requests, orchestrate calls across the internal services that do the ranking and retrieval, interpret their responses, and assemble the final response the customer sees. We also own the public configuration APIs customers use to control how discovery behaves, and the MCP layer that exposes all of it to AI agents.

Our team owns both platform & product components: Because of the positioning of our services, we take part in every architectural decision of our core product offering. At the same time, our goals are heavily influenced by direct customer feedback, because all product discovery-related features are either implemented in or integrated with our services.

All of our services are public APIs, so interface design and backward compatibility are a constant part of the job. But most of our attention goes to keeping them fast and up: we serve up to 15k RPS, fan out to many internal services on every request, and are expected to stay available and degrade gracefully when any of them fails or slows down.

The work is distributed systems in practice rather than in theory: request orchestration, failure isolation, caching, latency budgets, capacity planning, and the observability to know what is actually happening in production. The team is small enough that engineers own problems end to end, from design through on-call.

About you

You're a senior engineer who wants to own features end to end, not just close tickets. You've built and run production Python services, ideally high-traffic or latency-sensitive ones, and you've been on-call for them. You think in trade-offs: latency versus cost, a quick fix versus a durable one, a new parameter versus a public API customers can't afford to see break. You can take a feature from a rough problem statement to a design, ship it, and then make sure it behaves in production. You're comfortable leading a project with one or two other engineers and helping teammates grow along the way. When a problem is only partly defined, you ask the right questions to pin it down. When you meet an unfamiliar protocol or system, you read the spec and work out how it fits. You change your mind when someone has a better argument, and you still care about your code long after it merges.

What you will do

- Own the design and delivery of features and components in our services.

- Design and evolve public API endpoints with backward compatibility in mind, and contribute to architecture discussions for our services.

- Improve performance and reliability: find latency and failure hotspots, add the observability needed to understand them, and fix them.

- Take an active part in design and code review, and mentor mid-level engineers.

- Work with product, solutions/support, and other engineering teams to understand customer needs and turn them into solid technical solutions

- Take part in on-call for the systems you own, and lead incident response and follow-through when things break.

What we are looking for

Technical

- Solid experience building and operating backend services in production, ideally high-traffic or low-latency ones.

- Extensive Python knowledge (our primary language).

- Hands-on experience with observability (metrics, logs, traces) and debugging performance issues in live systems.

- Experience designing and evolving public APIs that external customers depend on.

- Experience designing & implementing scalable service-oriented architectures.

Beyond the code

- Track record of delivering projects end to end, including leading small efforts with other engineers.

- Collaborative mindset: open to feedback, and willing to change your position when someone has a better argument.

- Clear written communication - design docs, RFCs, postmortems.

- Good judgment about trade-offs and scope.

- Comfort with ambiguity and loosely defined problems.

- Ownership that extends past merge, to how the system behaves in production.

Nice to have

- Experience with AWS

- Background in search, ranking, information retrieval, or e-commerce product discovery.

- Exposure to AI/LLM-facing infrastructure (MCP, agent tooling, or similar).

Benefits

🏝️ Unlimited vacation time - we strongly encourage all of our employees take at least 3 weeks per year

🌎 Fully remote team - choose where you live

🛋️ Work from home stipend! We want you to have the resources you need to set up your home office

💻 Apple laptops provided for new employees

🧑‍🎓 Training and development budget for every employee, refreshed each year

👪 Maternity & Paternity leave for qualified employees

🧠 Work with smart people who will help you grow and make a meaningful impact

💵 Base salary: $80k–$120k USD, depending on knowledge, skills, experience, and interview results TBD

📈 Stock options - offered in addition to the base salary

🎉 Regular team offsites to connect and collaborate

Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion at Constructor

At Constructor.io we are committed to cultivating a work environment that is diverse, equitable, and inclusive. As an equal opportunity employer, we welcome individuals of all backgrounds and provide equal opportunities to all applicants regardless of their education, diversity of opinion, race, color, religion, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, veteran status or affiliation in any other protected group.

Studies have shown that women and people of color may be less likely to apply for jobs unless they meet every one of the qualifications listed. Our primary interest is in finding the best candidate for the job. We encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet all of our listed qualifications.

title: Staff Backend Engineer - Operations Tech Team
description:
Staff Backend Engineer - Operations Tech Team

Hybrid in London, UK

We’re looking for a Staff Backend Engineer to join the Operations Tech team. 

You’ll influence the technical direction of iwoca’s in-house CRM and build parts of it yourself – the system that hundreds of staff across sales, account management, credit, and collections use to give our customers five-star service.

The company 

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

The team 

The Operations Tech team builds the tools iwoca’s UK operations teams use every day: the CRM, and the systems behind phone calls, emails, notifications, and task management. Those tools are a competitive advantage – they help colleagues manage risk and enable the outstanding customer service that sets iwoca apart.

The team works closely with the Operations Strategy team, which sets operational priorities and scopes much of the tooling. Many of its users work in the same building, and you’ll see how your changes affect the people you work with.

We’re growing the team to ten engineers (including this role), two of them tech leads, and two product owners. Most of its time goes on quarterly roadmap projects, alongside a support rota, and regular small feature improvements.

The role 

As a staff backend engineer, you’ll take whole projects end to end: work out what operations teams need, design it, build it, and look after it in production. You’ll decide with the tech leads where the CRM’s service boundaries sit and how to model each domain’s data. You’ll judge your work by what it changes for those teams and their customers.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role with no line management, but you’ll mentor the engineers around you. You’ll often pair with a more junior engineer, share what you know, and set the standards the team works to through design discussions and code review.

You’ll learn how iwoca lends, from credit decisions to collections and financial crime. The team is adding AI to the CRM’s workflows, and you’ll have a say in where it helps.

Live project examples:

- Migrating the monolith. Moving CRM functionality out of iwoca’s Django monolith into separate services, such as customer contact and phone calls, that deploy and scale on their own.

- Building customer-facing AI agents to take the load off our teams as we grow, and the infrastructure to make them reliable and trustworthy

- Improving our onboarding journey to so that there’s less manual work getting a customer their funds, for example using LLMs to speed up compliance checks

- Credit card operations. Building the CRM services that let operations teams support customers on iwoca’s business credit card.

- iwocaChat. Extending the Claude-powered assistant that answers operations staff questions about a customer, using data held across several systems.

The requirements 

Essential:

- System design. You’ve designed large production systems and the domain models at their core, and changed their architecture while people relied on them.

- Backend engineering. You have deep expertise in at least one object-oriented language. You’ve written and run backend services in it.

- Technical leadership. You’ve led technical decisions across a team as an individual contributor, and helped other engineers grow through code reviews and design sessions.

- Operational problems. You’ve worked with non-technical colleagues to understand a problem they had, and built the system that solved it.

- AI leverage. You’ve built agentic workflows, or used AI to scale your engineering output beyond what you could deliver alone. You judge when to use it and when not to, and you check its output before it reaches production.

- Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail to your audience.

Bonus:

- Python stack. You’ve worked with Python, Django, Celery, and PostgreSQL.

- Full-stack. You’ve contributed to frontend codebases, particularly in React or TypeScript.

- Monolith migration. You’ve moved functionality out of a large monolith into separate services, while both stayed in production.

- Asynchronous systems. You’ve built services that communicate through message queues such as RabbitMQ.

- Contact systems. You’ve worked on telephony, email, or messaging systems, such as Twilio.

- Models in production systems. You’ve built systems that use model outputs to make operational decisions, such as which work to prioritise.

The salary 

We expect to pay from £100,000 to £130,000 for this role. But, we're open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.

The culture 

At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective.

We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better. We provide the infrastructure where every iwocan always has access to the best models and where those models have access to all of our data. We will help our people to learn how to use and grow with the new tools available to them.

The offices 

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

- Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

- Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits 

- Flexible working hours.

- Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.

- A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.

- 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.

- A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.

- Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.

- 3% Pension contributions on total earnings.

- An employee equity incentive scheme.

- Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.

- Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme.

- Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:

- A learning and development budget for everyone.

- Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers.

- Access to learning platforms like Treehouse.

Wir bei Knuddels haben uns das Ziel gesetzt, soziale Netzwerke wieder wirklich sozial zu machen - mit echter menschlicher Nähe statt bloßen Content-Konsums. In unserer Community soll jedes Mitglied 3 wichtige Menschen für sein echtes Leben finden: Jobtitel sind dir nicht wichtig und du möchtest dazu beitragen, unsere Vision zu erreichen? Wir wollen dich kennenlernen. 

Du bist der Ansicht, du könntest gut zu unserem Unternehmen und in unser Team passen? Dann bewirb dich mit deinen Unterlagen und wir finden gemeinsam heraus, wie und wo wir dich am besten einsetzen können. 

Was bieten wir dir? 

- Wachstum nach deinen Vorstellungen - Ob Fach- oder Führungskarriere: bei uns gestaltest du deinen individuellen Entwicklungspfad mit. 

- Team-Unterstützung durch Gespräche, Coaching, Feedback und Mentoring - Wir leben eine offene Kultur mit ehrlichem, konstruktivem Austausch und starkem Zusammenhalt. 

- Flache Hierarchien und Mitsprache - Bei uns zählt jede Stimme: gestalte aktiv mit und bring deine Ideen ein. 

- Flexibilität, die sich deinem Leben anpasst - Home Office, spontane Arzttermine oder kurzfristiger Urlaub: wir vertrauen auf Selbstorganisation. 

- Büro in Top-Lage mit kostenlosem Frühstück und Mittagessen, Fitness, Mystery Lunch (zweiwöchentliches Mittagessen mit einem zufälligen Teammitglied), Workshops und wunderschöner Dachterrasse - Unsere Arbeitsumgebung bietet alles für Wohlbefinden und kreative Energie. 

- Direktes Feedback von Endnutzern (B2C-Company) - Du siehst unmittelbar, wie dein Beitrag bei unseren Nutzer:innen ankommt. 

- Fokus auf unser eigenes Produkt - Eine einzigartige Community-Plattform, die Menschen näher zusammenbringt, mit Sinn und Wirkung. 

- alle Benefits findest auch nochmal unter jobs.knuddels.de 

Was bieten wir nicht? 

- Staubige Konzernstrukturen

- Arbeiten an Geschäftskundenprojekten (Wir sind ein B2C-Unternehmen)

- Einen an den Haaren herbei gezogenen dritten Bullet Point, wenn uns nur zwei einfallen :)

- Du befindest dich mind. im 3. Semester in Informatik, Mathematik oder eines vergleichbaren Studiengangs oder du konntest anderweitig schon relevante Programmiererfahrung sammeln

- Idealerweise hast du Erfahrung mit einer oder mehreren der folgenden Technologien

- TypeScript

- React

- Java

- Svelte

- PostgreSQL

- Python

- Du hast Freude am analytischen Denken

- Du hast ein hohes Maß an Selbständigkeit, Selbstorganisation und Motivation

- Du hast großen Spaß an der Arbeit im Team

Abhängig von deinen Fähigkeiten und Erfahrungen finden wir die passende Stelle für dich in unserem Team.

title: Senior Gen AI Software Engineer
description:
Liftoff is a leading AI-powered performance marketing platform for the mobile app economy. Our end-to-end technology stack helps app marketers acquire and retain high-value users, while enabling publishers to maximize revenue across programmatic and direct demand.

Liftoff’s solutions, including Accelerate, Direct, Monetize, Intelligence, and Vungle Exchange, support over 6,600 mobile businesses across 74 countries in sectors such as gaming, social, finance, ecommerce, and entertainment. Founded in 2012 and headquartered in Redwood City, CA, Liftoff has a diverse, global presence.

Join Liftoff as a Senior Gen AI Software Engineer and help shape the future of ad tech. As a key member of our Gen AI team, you’ll design and build AI-powered products for our demand-side business, helping teams turn complex data into better decisions and meaningful customer growth.

You’ll work across the stack, building intelligent systems and data pipelines in Python, alongside the TypeScript and React experiences that bring those capabilities to users. You’ll partner closely with product, engineering, and customer-facing teams to identify high-impact opportunities, move quickly from prototype to production, and continuously improve what you ship.

This is a hands-on role for an engineer who enjoys working at the intersection of AI, product, and software engineering. You’ll help define how Liftoff applies modern AI to real business problems, balancing experimentation with the judgment and engineering discipline needed to build useful, reliable products.

This role is ideal for an engineer who thrives in ambiguity, enjoys experimenting with new technology, and is motivated by turning promising AI capabilities into products that create real value. You’ll tackle complex problems, validate new approaches, and drive meaningful improvements across Liftoff.

WHAT YOU'LL DO 

- Own generative AI product capabilities end to end, from understanding user workflows and prototyping an approach through implementation, rollout, measurement, and ongoing improvement.

- Rapidly prototype and validate AI solutions, using focused experiments to test user value and technical feasibility, then turn what works into production-ready capabilities.

- Build agentic workflows that can reason over campaign, customer, creative, and performance data, use well-defined tools, produce structured results, and hand control back to a person when appropriate.

- Partner closely with decision makers and subject matter experts to understand their workflows, constraints, and business context, then integrate AI agents into daily work in practical and useful ways.

- Design how AI systems access and use relevant information, including the data, tools, and instructions needed to produce useful grounded results.

- Build the systems that make AI workflows reliable in production, including tool use, state management, failure recovery, and appropriate boundaries for human review.

- Define clear, testable interfaces between models and software so uncertain model behavior can be handled safely within dependable product systems.

- Develop evaluation systems that measure whether AI features accomplish the intended task, using realistic examples and an appropriate combination of automated checks and human judgment.

- Build the instrumentation needed to understand quality, adoption, business impact, latency, cost, and failure modes in production.

- Apply appropriate safeguards for customer data, system access, and high-impact workflows.

- Build the Python services and TypeScript and React interfaces that turn these capabilities into cohesive products for customer facing teams.

- Evaluate new models and techniques pragmatically, adopting them when they materially improve product quality, capability, speed, or cost.

- Mentor other engineers and help establish shared practices for designing, testing, and operating AI-powered products.

WHO YOU ARE 

- Minimum Bachelors Degree and 8 yrs of relevant experience.

- You are a seasoned software engineer who has built and operated meaningful production products, ideally including zero-to-one work spanning backend services, data, and user interfaces.

- You have shipped LLM-powered or AI-assisted products beyond a demo and understand the practical challenges of reliability, context, tool use, provider changes, latency, cost, and changing model behavior.

- You are highly proficient in Python and comfortable working in TypeScript and React, with strong fundamentals in API design, data modeling, SQL, and testing.

- You understand how to build the broader system around a model, including its data, tools, instructions, permissions, feedback loops, and measures of quality.

- You can define success criteria, investigate failures, and use testing, feedback, and production signals to improve AI experiences over time.

- You exercise strong product and engineering judgment, choosing when a problem calls for traditional software, an LLM-powered approach, or a thoughtful combination of both.

- You communicate complex technical ideas clearly and collaborate effectively with domain experts and non-technical partners.

- You are comfortable working through ambiguity, making informed decisions with incomplete information, and changing direction when evidence shows a better path.

- You are a lifelong learner with strong but flexible opinions, and you thrive on giving and receiving constructive feedback.

Helpful, but not required

- Experience as an early engineer, startup founder, or in a similarly high-ownership environment where you moved quickly from ambiguous problems to shipped products.

- Experience with advertising technology, campaign optimization, performance marketing, analytics products, or other data-rich B2B software.

Location: 

The preferred location for the role is in Pacific Standard Time Zone. This role is eligible for full-time remote work in one of our entities: CA, CO, ID, IL, FL, GA, MA, MI, MN, MO, NJ, NV, NY, OR, PA, TX, UT, and WA.

We are a remote-first company with US hubs in Redwood City, Los Angeles, and New York City. 

Travel Expectations: 

We offer several opportunities for in-person team gatherings, including but not limited to project meetings, regional meetups, and company-wide events. We expect our employees to attend these gatherings at least once per quarter. These gatherings provide essential opportunities for collaboration, communication, and team building.

Compensation :

Liftoff offers all employees a full compensation package that includes equity and health/vision/dental benefits associated with your country of residence. Base compensation will vary based on the candidate's location and experience. 

The following are our base salary ranges for multiple levels:

- SF Bay Area, Los Angeles/Orange County, NYC, Seattle: $230,000 - $270,000

- All other cities and towns in our approved states: $211,000 - $248,000

#LI-VM1

Liftoff offers a fast-paced, collaborative, and innovative work environment where employees are empowered to grow and make an impact. We’re shaping the future of the mobile app ecosystem—join us and help accelerate what’s next.

Liftoff’s compensation strategy includes competitive salaries, equity, and benefits designed to support employee well-being and performance. We benchmark compensation based on role, level, and location to ensure fairness and market alignment. Benefits may include medical coverage, wellness stipends, and additional perks based on your country of residence.

Liftoff is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and applicants regardless of race, ethnicity, national origin, age, marital status, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Agency and Third Party Recruiter Notice: 

Liftoff does not accept unsolicited resumes from individual recruiters or third-party recruiting agencies in response to job postings. No fee will be paid to third parties who submit unsolicited candidates directly to our hiring managers or Recruiting Team. All candidates must be submitted via our Applicant Tracking System by approved Liftoff vendors who have been expressly requested to make a submission by our Recruiting Team for a specific job opening. No placement fees will be paid to any firm unless such a request has been made by the Liftoff Recruiting Team and such a candidate was submitted to the Liftoff Recruiting Team via our Applicant Tracking System.

title: Senior Full Stack
description:
Headquarters: Tallinn, Estonia

URL: https://toggl.com/jobs/ 

We are looking for a Senior Full Stack Engineer to join one of our Product Tribes, the cross-functional units that own the end-to-end experience for a specific Toggl user role. You'll join the Tribe building for managers, the people who plan work, protect margins, and keep projects on time and on budget.

You own significant parts of that experience end-to-end, working hands-on with product and design to ship work that matters. You'll do this as we build and launch Toggl 2.0, our consolidated planning, time tracking, and time intelligence product.

The salary for this position is €83,000 annually. 

You can work from anywhere in the world as long as your main location is between UTC-4 and UTC+4. 

The Role 

As a Senior Full Stack Engineer, you own meaningful parts of the product end-to-end, from the data model and the API to the interface someone actually clicks: the technical approach, the quality of what ships, and whether it actually works for the people using it. You are accountable not for tickets closed, but for clarity, craft, and outcomes.

You'll work in the Tribe serving managers, across planning and capacity management, dashboards, and billable work. This is some of the most data-dense, interaction-heavy surface area in the product: schedules and capacity views, reports, and visualizations that have to stay fast and readable at real customer scale. The interesting problems live on both sides of the API here - the query behind a capacity view matters as much as how that view renders. You'll build with React and TypeScript on the frontend and our backend services (mostly Golang) and data layer (Postgres) behind them, alongside a product manager, a designer, and engineers who are used to owning their work and pushing back when something isn't right. In a tribe of 5 other engineers, your impact and visibility are high.

Our team meetings are scheduled between 11:00 and 16:00 UTC. Your availability and commitment to participate in these sessions are essential for effective collaboration and team alignment.

Your main responsibilities will be:

Ownership and delivery 

- 
Take projects from problem to production. Own the technical approach for major features front to back, break the work down sensibly, sequence it, and ship in slices rather than one big drop.

- 
Make the technical calls in your area. Choose between options, name the tradeoffs, and decide without waiting for permission or escalating routine judgment.

- 
Keep your work visible without being chased. Flag risks and slips early, keep the Tribe in the loop, and unblock yourself.

Craft and quality across the stack 

- 
Build interfaces people trust with dense, real-world data. Planning views, dashboards, and reports that stay fast, accessible, and readable when the dataset gets ugly.

- 
Design the data and API layer those views depend on. Model it so the feature you're building now doesn't make the next three harder.

- 
Own performance as a feature, end to end. Profile, measure, and fix the slow query and the slow render instead of hoping the data stays small.

- 
Write code others can work in. Sensible components and services, real test coverage where it earns its keep, and a codebase that's easier to change after you touch it.

Working with product and design 

- 
Shape solutions, don't just implement them. Push on the problem, question requirements that don't hold up, and propose simpler paths when you see one.

- 
Partner closely with design. Prototype early, spot the edge cases in a flow before it's built, and hold the bar on UX quality with your designer rather than after handoff.

- 
Stay close to users and evidence. Join user tests, read the feedback, look at the data, and let it change what you build.

Raising the bar 

- 
Review code with intent. Give precise, actionable feedback that makes the change and the person better.

- 
Mentor and interview. Help other engineers grow, and help us hire well.

- 
Improve things across team boundaries. Spot shared components and duplicated work between Tribes, and raise it before we build the same thing twice.

AI as core leverage 

- 
Use AI tools extensively in your daily work for exploration, prototyping, code generation and review, debugging, research, and writing. AI fluency is not optional. It's part of how you increase your speed, depth, and impact - and you're expected to help the rest of the Tribe get better at it too.

About You 

You will thrive in this role if you:

- 
Have significant experience building and shipping production web applications end to end, and can lead major projects rather than just contribute to them.

- 
Are genuinely comfortable on both sides of the stack. You're deep on one side and properly capable on the other, not someone who hands off at the API boundary.

- 
Have deep, practical knowledge of JavaScript, TypeScript, React, and modern CSS - including state management and side-effect handling in large applications.

- 
Are solid on backend fundamentals: at least one backend language you know well, API design, relational data modelling, and enough instinct for query performance to spot the problem before production does. Prior Golang experience is not mandatory but you have to be willing to adopt it and become comfortable with it fast. 

- 
Hold an extremely high bar for quality. You know what great looks like, you notice the details others miss, and you don't ship work you wouldn't put your name on.

- 
Have a knack for data-heavy product surfaces - performance, readability, and the principles behind a chart that actually communicates something.

- 
Care about the user's problem, not just the ticket. You start from what someone is trying to get done and work back to the implementation.

- 
Own outcomes, not output. You follow your work into production, watch how it behaves, and fix what needs fixing.

- 
Thrive in ambiguity and move fast. You make confident decisions with incomplete information, adapt when things change, and course-correct without drama.

- 
Are hands-on with AI tools. You actively use AI as a core part of how you build, not a side experiment, and you have opinions about where it helps and where it doesn't.

- 
Don't need to be managed. You set your own direction, keep people in the loop, and ask for help when it matters.

- 
Have excellent written and verbal English communication skills. You write clearly, explain technical tradeoffs to non-engineers without jargon, and default to async communication that others can follow.

- 
Are eager to contribute to the engineering team's growth - code review, mentoring, and interviewing included.

- 
Value transparency, ownership, and speed over perfection. You ship, learn, and improve rather than waiting for the perfect plan.

- 
Nice to have: 

- 
Experience with TanStack is a bonus, and so is a real understanding of frontend caching and eventual consistency, we'd love to hire someone who's dealt with that tradeoff directly.

- 
Experience with capacity planning, scheduling, reporting, or other complex B2B SaaS products.

- 
Experience working with distributed or microservice systems, a basic understanding of infrastructure and infrastructure as code, and some experience creating, improving, or debugging CI/CD pipelines.

This Role Is NOT 

- 
A ticket-taker role. If you want fully specced work handed to you, this isn't the right fit.

- 
A pixel-pusher translating finished designs into code with no say in the problem or the solution.

- 
A role where you hand off at the API boundary. If "that's a backend ticket" is your instinct, this will frustrate you.

- 
A role where quality is someone else's job. Toggl doesn't have a dedicated QA
team or layer: there's no separate team that will catch your bugs, write your
tests, or own your performance regressions.

- 
A place to work in isolation from users. You'll be expected to know who you're building for and why.

- 
A role for people who need heavy process, frequent approvals, or top-down direction to do their best work.

The Team 

We are a global team of ~80 awesome people working from over 40 countries around the globe. We hire globally, you work locally—in the heart of London, a beach outside of Río de Janeiro, or a quiet village near Florence, the choice is yours. Every few months we travel to meet up somewhere in the world and spend some quality time together. We place a huge amount of trust in our people, and we measure the outcomes rather than the work itself. Our values fuel our results.

What's Happening at Toggl 

Toggl is at an exciting turning point. We're taking our best-in-class time tracking - trusted and loved by millions of users worldwide - and expanding it into something bigger: Toggl 2.0 . One product that brings together time tracking, planning, capacity management, reporting, and insight. The idea is simple: better time tracking creates better data, which powers everything else. We call it time intelligence. We build with AI throughout, and we think it's a real multiplier for strong engineers rather than a substitute for them. The judgment, the tradeoffs, and the accountability for what ships stay with people.

Benefits 

- 
Freedom to choose when and how much you work—we only measure results

- 
24 days of paid time off a year, plus your local holidays

- 
Unlimited sick leave

- 
In-person meetups for team-building (expenses covered)

- 
4-6 weeks paid sabbatical (depending on tenure)

- 
Laptop budget up to 2,500€ and it renews every 3 years

- 
€2,000 budget to set up your home office and an additional €300 every year after 3 years of tenure

- 
€3,000 per year for co-working space membership and/or internet service at home

- 
€4,000 per year contribution to use for training, workshops, and conferences

- 
€2,400 per year contribution for any equipment or services to improve and/or maintain your physical and mental health

- 
Support for buying tools you need for doing your best work (even eyeglasses if you need a new pair)

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/toggl-senior-full-stack

title: Senior Software Engineer, Supply
description:
Streaming TV is no longer just a brand awareness channel. It’s becoming a core part of the performance marketing mix, alongside search and social. Vibe.co is building the platform that makes TV work like the rest of the acquisition stack: targeted, measurable, and optimized for results.

Vibe.co is an Audience First Streaming TV Advertising platform that gives marketers the tools to reach the right audiences, optimize campaigns in real time, and understand what’s actually driving business outcomes. With hyper-targeted segmentation, AI-powered recommendations, real-time optimization, and incrementality measurement, Vibe brings the precision and accountability of digital advertising to the biggest screen in the house.

Today, more than 12,000 brands use Vibe.co to reach 120 million+ households. And in August 2026, Vibe.co became a Walmart company, opening up a new chapter for the business and the industry. With Walmart’s first-party data and purchase signals now part of the Vibe platform, advertisers can connect TV advertising to real-world transactions and measure the impact of CTV with a level of precision previously associated with platforms like Google and Meta.

This is a unique moment to join Vibe. With Walmart’s scale, data, and reach behind us, we’re building the next generation of TV advertising and creating a more measurable, performance-driven future for the channel.

Your team

You will join the Supply team, which owns Vibe's inventory: the publishers we partner with, the deals we run, and the catalog of apps, channels and shows our advertisers care about.

Shows are the reason people turn on their TV. Advertisers don't just want impressions: they want to show up next to the right shows, live sports and premium channels. Supply brings that content to Vibe through direct publisher partnerships, curated deals and sponsorships. It makes it easy to find, understand and buy, through real-time bidding, or any technology the publisher uses.

Premium publishers care as much about which ads run on their shows as about who buys them, and great creatives are what earn us access.

The team brings together partnerships, operations, and product. You will work closely with the DSP team, which runs the bidding infrastructure, and the Performance team, which decides how to value each opportunity, as well as with publisher partners directly.

Your mission

As a Senior Software Engineer on Supply, you will build the systems that let Vibe grow, operate, and trust its inventory. You will turn publisher partnerships into live, healthy supply, and give the business and our partners the tools to manage it at scale.

What you will do

Publisher integrations 

- Build and improve publisher integrations end-to-end, from onboarding a new partner to supporting new ad formats and sponsorship offers.

- Implement measurement requirements with publishers and the DSP team (e.g. UID2, publisher IDs) so the bidder sees richer inventory.

- Own integration health: detect broken or degraded supply before it costs us spend.

Deals & catalog 

- Build the services behind deal setup, catalog management, and price configuration, in partnership with DSP on the deal API.

- Automate the routine work of the Supply team (new deals, stale-supply cleanup, troubleshooting) so it scales with the number of partners, and with Vibe.

- Enrich the catalog with content data (shows, genres, live events, channels) so advertisers can find what they are looking for, and even enjoy looking for it.

Supply tooling & publisher platform 

- Build real-time monitoring, alerting, and analytics on supply volume, quality, and spend.

- Build publisher-facing features: reporting, insights, and self-serve catalog tools.

What we're looking for

- 5+ years of experience as a software engineer building and operating backend systems in production.

- Strong programming skills (Go, Python and/or Rust), with real engineering discipline: testing, code review, CI/CD, maintainable design.

- Hands-on with AI coding tools (Claude Code, Codex or similar) in your day-to-day engineering workflow.

- Experience integrating with external partners' systems and APIs, and owning those integrations when they break.

- Comfortable owning services from code to production: cloud infrastructure (AWS or GCP), Kubernetes, and the observability to know your systems are healthy.

- Product sense: you like talking to the people who use what you build, and you turn ambiguous business needs into concrete deliverables.

- Excellent communication in English, with internal teams and with partners' technical contacts.

- Pragmatism over purity: a bias toward shipping value.

Nice to have

- Experience in AdTech or programmatic: OpenRTB, SSPs, PMP / PG deals, VAST.

- Knowledge of the CTV ecosystem (publishers, apps, FAST channels).

- Experience with identity solutions (UID2 or similar).

- Experience building partner-facing or B2B dashboards and reporting.

Our Values 

At Vibe, we run on three values: Impact, Ambition, and Urgency. We tie every goal to a real business outcome, think 10x rather than settling for good enough, and move daily rather than waiting for perfect conditions.

You’ll thrive here if you own outcomes without needing direction, default to action, and hold yourself to results, not effort.

This is a high-performance environment with high-performance rewards: you’ll work alongside people who push you, with real ownership over hard problems in a market that’s moving fast.

If that sounds like the best version of your career, we want to meet you.

What We Offer 

The base pay range for this role in Paris is €90,000 – €125,000. We will support relocation to Paris for great candidates.

The base pay range for this role in New York is $140,000 – $200,000. We will support relocation to New York for great candidates.

At Vibe, we want you to build something, own something, and grow fast. Here’s how we back that up:

- Variable pay — Based on real Vibe business goals.

- Hybrid flexibility — We’re in the Heart of Paris and our team is in 3x a week!

- Health insurance — Full coverage via Alan.

- Meal vouchers — Via Swile.

- Annual offsite — The whole team, once a year, somewhere worth the trip.

- Tech Syncs — Engineering and Product meet in person at least quarterly, worldwide.

Our Interview Process 

We respect your time. Here’s exactly what to expect, no surprises, no ghosting.

- Recruiter Screen — 30 minutes. We’ll share more context on the role and team, and learn more about your background and what you’re looking for.

- Hiring Manager Interview — 45 minutes. Meet with the person you’d work with directly and dive deeper into your experience, product background, and approach to the role.

- Technical Discussion — 90 minutes. A deeper conversation covering product thinking, measurement methodology, data reasoning, and a use case relevant to the role.

- Bar Raiser Interview — 30 minutes. Meet with a senior leader at Vibe for a final conversation and an opportunity to ask any remaining questions.

- Offer — We move quickly once we’ve made a decision. We don’t let good decisions sit.

Equal Opportunity 

Vibe is an equal opportunity employer. We evaluate all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

We believe the best ideas come from teams with different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences. If you need a reasonable accommodation during the application or interview process, please let us know.

Referral Instructions 

Being referred? Ask your contact to submit your application directly on your behalf.

title: Backend Software Engineer
description:
About Wayflyer 

Today's small businesses need a capital provider that keeps pace with their growth ambitions. Traditional financing options are slow, cumbersome and often out of reach. That's why we built Wayflyer.

Our technology allows us to assess businesses in minutes, generate financing offers that reflect their growth potential and send funds in as little as 24 hours. To date, we've deployed over $6bn to thousands of businesses worldwide, backed by Tier 1 banks like J.P. Morgan.

You'll be collaborating with ambitious colleagues from around the world. We have offices in Dublin, London, New York, Charlotte, Berlin and Sydney.

The challenge 

We assess businesses in minutes and send funds in as little as 24 hours. The systems that make that possible need to be fast, reliable, and built to scale as we grow into new markets. 

What you'll actually do 

- 
Design and develop scalable backend services using Python and Django, focusing on our core financial products

- 
Build and maintain RESTful APIs that power our customer-facing applications and internal tools

- 
Implement robust data models and database schemas to support our financial services infrastructure

- 
Write clean, testable code with comprehensive unit and integration tests

- 
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to design and implement new features and improvements

- 
Optimize application performance and ensure high availability of our services

- 
Participate in code reviews and contribute to technical documentation

- 
Monitor and maintain production systems, ensuring reliability and security

Who thrives here 

You should be comfortable making and defending technical decisions, while remaining open to feedback and alternative approaches. You'll need to balance technical excellence with business needs and help guide the team toward pragmatic solutions.

You excel at stakeholder management and can effectively communicate technical concepts to non-technical audiences. You're proactive in identifying and addressing potential issues before they become problems.

We look for candidates with most or all of the below traits that can point to real experience applying them.

- 
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related field, or equivalent practical experience

- 
5+ years of professional experience in backend development with Python

- 
Strong proficiency in Django, or other Python API frameworks (e.g. FastAPI, Flask)

- 
Experience with SQL databases (preferably PostgreSQL) and ORM frameworks

- 
Knowledge of API design principles and microservices architecture

- 
Experience with AWS or similar cloud platforms

- 
Solid understanding of version control with Git

- 
Experience with testing frameworks (e.g., pytest, unittest)

- 
Understanding of security best practices and data protection

- 
Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail

- 
Excellent communication abilities and proven track record of successful team collaboration

Given what we do, experience in financial services, fintech and business-to-business organisations is particularly interesting to us.

We hire for range 

What you're like as a person and how you treat people is a big deal for us. People love working with you. You're helpful and generous with your time and knowledge. People love helping you back. People know where they stand with you.

You're always looking to learn and grow, on a personal and professional level. And you're always looking to help others learn and grow by sharing your own knowledge and experience.

You know why diversity, equality, inclusion and belonging matters, and speak up when we can do better.

What this role could turn into 

Engineers here tend to grow in the direction they're most interested in - whether that's deepening technical specialism, moving into architecture, or taking on more cross-functional ownership as we scale. 

Location and working policy 

📍 Fully remote, Europe.

The good stuff 

25 days off, plus public holidays, onboarding in our Dublin or London office. Equity - because you should own a piece of what you're building. Generous parental leave for primary and secondary caregivers. 60 days a year to work abroad from wherever you want.

By submitting your application, you acknowledge that Wayflyer Limited will process your personal data for the purpose of evaluating your suitability for the role. Such processing is based on the need to take steps prior to entering into a potential employment agreement. To learn more about how we handle your personal data, you can contact our privacy team at privacy@wayflyer.com or review our privacy notice at https://wayflyer.com/privacy-notice .

title: Senior Space Systems Engineer, Mission Optimization
description:
Welcome to Planet. We believe in using space to help life on Earth. 

Planet designs, builds, and operates the largest constellation of imaging satellites in history. This constellation delivers an unprecedented dataset of empirical information via a revolutionary cloud-based platform to authoritative figures in commercial, environmental, and humanitarian sectors. We are both a space company and data company all rolled into one.

Customers and users across the globe use Planet's data to develop new technologies, drive revenue, power research, and solve our world’s toughest obstacles.

As we control every component of hardware design, manufacturing, data processing, and software engineering, our office is a truly inspiring mix of experts from a variety of domains.

We have a people-centric approach toward culture and community and we strive to iterate in a way that puts our team members first and prepares our company for growth. Join Planet and be a part of our mission to change the way people see the world.

title: Business Intelligence Analyst (Contractor)
description:
Headquarters: San Francisco, CA or Remote (U.S.)

**This is a contract role expected to last until April 15th, 2027 

Location : This role is Remote in the U.S., with the option to work onsite from our San Francisco, CA headquarters.

Visa sponsorship is not available for this role. 

About Doximity 

Doximity is the leading clinical AI company with the largest network of U.S. clinicians. Doximity’s AI-powered workflow platform is trusted by over 85% of U.S. physicians and 300+ health systems. Doximity's mission is to help clinicians be more productive so they can provide better care for their patients.

At Doximity, we value curiosity, ownership, inclusion, and a commitment to making a meaningful impact. If you're excited about solving complex problems that improve healthcare, we'd love to hear from you.

About the Role 

As a Business Intelligence Analyst , you will:

- Work closely with our Product, Strategic Analytics, Client Success, and Sales teams to create client-facing analyses.

- Showcase your engineering skills by creating data products from scratch and automating code so they can be re-used by other teammates.

- Continue to improve your technical and non-technical skill sets.

- Leverage Doximity's extensive datasets to identify and classify behavioral patterns of medical professionals on our platform.

- Grow into a presentation/communication-focused role or dive deeper into more-involved technical challenges—the choice is yours.

What We're Looking For 

We're excited to meet candidates who have many of the following qualifications:

Must have: 

- Three (3) years of experience illustrating collaboration, passion for data, reliability, precision, curiosity, and respect for teammates and clients.

- Excellent SQL skills with proven ability to create and evaluate complex SQL statements involving numerous tables and complex relationships.

- Fluent in Python and experience using common modules (numpy, pandas, statsmodels, matplotlib) for EDA.

- Experience collaborating with non-technical stakeholders.

Nice to have: 

- Working knowledge of statistics and visualization.

- Experience working with data visualization tools.

- Advanced Excel skills.

- Experience using AI coding assistants and building AI-leveraged workflows.

- Experience working in the healthcare industry.

- Experience presenting data to a non-technical audience.

The Core Values of the Client Intelligence team

- Collaboration —The best candidates and teammates are not only strong in their own aptitudes but care deeply about supporting each other's growth.

- Passion for Data —You’re going to help our clients and team members with data-driven decision making. We need someone that can manipulate millions of rows of data and also ask the right questions to find the important insights.

- Reliability – Our team is efficient, flexible, and agile only because we trust the reliability of each member. We need self-starters and goal-oriented individuals for our continued success.

- Precision – Our team's deliverables power client analysis and inform real-world decisions. A successful candidate will triple check their work and their teammates' work, holding all of us to the highest data quality standards.

- Curiosity – Continuous learning is a cornerstone at Doximity, and curious individuals thrive in our environment. We’re looking for someone who is curious enough about data to go above-and-beyond the task for the true insight.

- Respect – A key dynamic that allows our team to flourish is respect: for ourselves and our quality of work, for our teammates, and for our internal clients who are under the pressure of deadlines and finance goals.

Why You'll Love Working Here 

At Doximity, you'll join a mission-driven company where your work has a meaningful impact on healthcare. We believe great ideas come from empowered teams, and we're committed to creating an environment where people can do their best work.

- Make a real impact. Help build products that support over a million healthcare professionals and ultimately improve patient care.

- Work with exceptional teammates. Collaborate with thoughtful, talented colleagues who value curiosity, humility, and continuous learning.

- Enjoy flexibility and trust. We support flexible ways of working and empower employees with the autonomy to own their work.

- Grow your career. Take on meaningful challenges, develop new skills, and shape your career through mentorship and professional development.

- Bring your authentic self. We're committed to fostering an inclusive culture where diverse perspectives are welcomed, respected, and celebrated.

- Coordinate with peer teams across Developer Experience, Infrastructure Platforms, and product groups to align priorities and timing.

- Lead AI-first development practices in how we build and what we ship, including AI skills and agent-assisted performance workflows.

- Mentor engineers in performance engineering, platform design, and technical decision-making.

- Serve as a performance expert for other teams and provide technical guidance on initiatives spanning multiple groups.

- Take part in on-call or operational support where your team's ownership model requires it.

- A track record of building and operating performance testing and analysis systems, with an understanding of where bottlenecks appear and how to find them.

- Experience leading or anchoring a performance enablement or platform function and achieving measurable adoption of internal tooling by influencing engineers and leaders who don't report to you.

- Experience defining and delivering a multi-quarter technical strategy or roadmap with engineering leadership.

- An AI-first development mindset demonstrated across the software lifecycle, including shaping how a team uses AI.

- Clear written, asynchronous communication, including explaining performance trade-offs to engineers and leadership.

Performance Enablement is part of Platform Enablement within Developer Experience and Infrastructure Platforms. We work asynchronously and collaborate broadly across R&D, coordinating with peer platform and product groups. Documentation, onboarding, and feedback loops help us turn early team engagements into capabilities that scale beyond individual teams.

title: Forward Deployed Engineer
description:
About Andercore 

Andercore is the AI-native supplier of industrial materials and goods for energy and infrastructure. We execute trade and distribution end-to-end, on our own account, at the speed of compute - and we are becoming the supplier of record for the entire industry.

Industrial procurement is a €900B market in Europe alone and the largest manual market on earth. 95% of customers have no direct access to global supply chains. Materials pass through four or five intermediaries before they reach a site, and 40% of the margin evaporates on the way. For decades, the operating system of this industry was people: people to source, negotiate, finance, ship, and sell.

We built the alternative from scratch. We are the supplier. We buy from global sources and sell to European customers on our own account. Our AI runs the full trade: sourcing, quality, pricing, sales, logistics, credit, and financing. One request. A firm quote in minutes. Delivered on time. For the customer, it feels like buying from their preferred local supplier. No warehouses. No fleet. No inventory risk. Every trade is pre-sold before it is bought.

We are also the credit counterparty. Customers are scored and insured in minutes and get up to 60 days of payment terms priced into the quote itself. The working capital behind every trade is bank-funded, not equity-funded.

Where we are today:

- Strong triple-digit-million euro turnover run rate, the majority of it from repeat customers

- Seven European markets live, sourced from suppliers across Asia and beyond

- 80+ people across Berlin (HQ), London, and Shanghai

- $90M raised in equity and debt, including our $40M Series B, from Atomico, Project A, Target Global, and Inven Capital - with working capital facilities from UniCredit and KfW

The margin is in the bits. The moat is in the atoms. We are building the supplier of record for industrial materials - and redefining how global trade works in one of the largest and most essential industries on earth.

Build where the work happens

As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you work side by side with the people who run our trade: sales, procurement, logistics, finance and customer success. You find where time and money go into manual work, and you build the agents, automations and tools that take it over.

Much of Andercore's daily work still happens in calls, emails, spreadsheets and PDFs. Our AI agents already schedule deliveries and request freight quotes; there is much more to do. You sit with the teams, understand their work in detail, ship a first version in days, and make it reliable enough that they trust it with real orders.

You work closely with our product engineers and the CPO. What works for one team, you turn into reusable skills and components the whole company can use, and you help our colleagues build with AI themselves.

What you will do

- Embed with the business: Spend real time with our commercial and operations teams and map how the work actually gets done. Find the steps that cost the most time, money or mistakes.

- Build and ship fast: Build agents, automations, internal tools and data flows, with a first version in days, not months. Bring what works into production together with our product engineers.

- Make agents reliable: Add evaluations, guardrails and human review where money or customers are involved. Monitor what you shipped and fix what breaks.

- Scale what works: Turn one-off solutions into reusable skills, knowledge bases and components. Help colleagues build with AI themselves.

- Close the loop: Measure impact: hours saved, error rates, speed and margin. Feed what you learn into the product roadmap.

- Be the bridge: Translate between the business and engineering. Write down decisions and trade-offs so others can build on them.

What success looks like

- Clear, measured time savings in the teams you work with

- Agents our colleagues trust with real orders

- Reusable skills and tools adopted across the company

- Business teams who build small automations themselves

- The best ideas from the field turned into product work

- Fewer errors in the steps you automated

What you bring

- At least 3 years of experience building and shipping software, ideally in Python or TypeScript.

- Hands-on experience building with LLMs or agent frameworks, and good judgment about where they work and where they don't.

- You enjoy working with non-technical colleagues: you ask good questions, listen, and explain things simply.

- Product sense: you turn a vague problem into a clear first version and improve it with real feedback.

- Solid data skills, including SQL, and comfort with messy real-world data such as emails, PDFs and spreadsheets.

- Speed with judgment: you ship quickly and know when something needs to be done properly.

- Experience in a startup or scale-up. Interest in trade, supply chain or B2B commerce is a plus.

- Fluent English. German is a plus.

We are an equal-opportunity employer and welcome applicants from all backgrounds, regardless of race, ethnicity, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, religion, age, disability, or any other characteristic. We believe that diversity drives innovation, creativity, and collective strength.
