title: Enterprise Success Manager, NL (EMEA)
description:
About Mistral 

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

The Role 

As an Enterprise Success Manager at Mistral, you own what happens to our most strategic enterprise accounts after the build: you make deployed AI stick in real workflows, keep production ARR healthy, defend renewals, and source the expansion signals Sales closes.

Mistral's Solutions teams create high-value AI use cases with our customers. Your job is to make those investments successful beyond delivery — adopting what has been built, operating it with confidence, measuring its business impact, and scaling value across the organization. You will work with customer sponsors, business teams, IT and security stakeholders, and across Mistral with Solutions, Product, Engineering and Support.

This is not a high-volume, ticket-queue customer success role. Portfolios are small and deep. It calls for a strategic account mindset, the technical judgment to navigate complex deployment environments, and the energy to build the customer success function as Mistral grows.

You will join on one of two tracks (and can move between them): 

- Adoption track — embedded in flagship transformations while Solutions is still delivering. You own the adoption and change-management motion around the build: user waves, enablement, champions, training programs, and the measurement that proves value is landing.

- Operational track — you take accounts through a structured handover once Solutions completes delivery, and own the run phase end-to-end: operational health, value realization, renewals, and expansion signals.

In both tracks you operate in close partnership with Solutions: they deliver and hand over; you own post-handover; they re-engage on expansion signals. Occasionally, account teams will also pull you into late-stage pre-sales — authoring the customer training and scale-up plan that gives a buyer confidence in the rollout, a motion already credited in a major European win.

What You Will Do 

Own the customer success and value plan

- Build a clear view of each account's objectives, stakeholders, deployed use cases, commitments and risks. Translate it into a shared success plan with owners, milestones and measurable outcomes.

- Establish a practical operating cadence with customer sponsors, business owners, IT and delivery teams. Lead success reviews that make progress, risks, decisions and next steps clear.

- Define a baseline and track the outcomes that matter for each use case: adoption and usage against entitled seats, customer satisfaction, operational health and business impact. Turn the evidence into a clear value narrative.

Make deployment realities part of the success plan

- Understand how each customer's deployment model — on-premises, VPC or serverless — affects the products and use cases they can access, operate and scale. Validate the specifics with the technical teams rather than assuming feature parity or identical operating models.

- Identify the practical implications of deployment choices: security and data requirements, access and integrations, release and upgrade cadence, available features, capacity, observability and support processes. Explain the trade-offs clearly to customer and Mistral stakeholders.

- Translate those constraints into an actionable adoption plan: align enablement and release communications with the version the customer actually runs, account for security approvals and upgrade windows, and agree how to measure usage when telemetry is limited.

- Spot risks early, qualify their impact on adoption, renewal or value, and coordinate the right Solutions, Product, Engineering or Support owners to resolve them. Set clear expectations without making unvalidated technical or roadmap commitments.

Drive adoption, autonomy and sustained value

- Help customer teams move from a delivered use case to regular, effective use. Identify the users, workflows and change-management needs that determine whether it sticks.

- Coordinate onboarding, training, product updates and hands-on enablement with the right Mistral and customer teams. Develop customer champions and train-the-trainer motions so adoption scales beyond direct Mistral involvement.

- Prepare the transition from delivery to run: clarify operational ownership, support and escalation paths, and the resources users need to succeed independently.

- Monitor adoption and customer health, investigate where usage or value is falling short, and lead a coordinated plan to address the causes.

Defend and grow the commercial relationship

- Own the renewal motion for your accounts: know every renewal date, the auto vs non-auto renewal terms, and the risk story behind each one. Run the renewal play early — no surprises at renewal time.

- Track and improve account NRR. Identify new use cases, teams and expansion opportunities, and share them with the account team grounded in demonstrated value.

- Lead business reviews with the account team: value delivered, risks owned, decisions needed, roadmap asks.

Bring the customer voice into Mistral

- Gather and qualify feedback from users, technical teams and sponsors. Distinguish enablement needs from product gaps, deployment constraints and support issues, and route each to the right owner.

- Track important requests and communicate progress and limitations back to the customer, while Product and Engineering retain ownership of product and technical decisions.

Build the company as well as the account

- Create the playbooks, success plans, handover practices and measurement approaches that are missing. Test them with customers, improve them, and make them reusable across accounts.

- Bring structure to ambiguity: identify what needs to happen, make a plan, mobilize the right people and follow through — without waiting for a perfect process or detailed instructions.

- Roughly a fifth of your time is protected, rotating build time for exactly this work; it is part of the job, not extra to it.

What We're Looking For 

- 5+ years of experience in customer-facing roles, such as Customer Success, Delivery/Implementation, or Solutions Consulting, ideally in a technical AI or SaaS environment.

- Experience owning outcomes for enterprise customers of technical products or deployed solutions — adoption and commercial outcomes (retention, renewal, expansion), not relationship management or activity reporting.

- Strong technical fluency in enterprise deployment models. You can identify what a deployment type (on-premises, VPC, serverless) means for available features, telemetry, upgrades and security reviews, and you validate specifics with technical teams instead of assuming parity.

- Ability to engage credibly with architects, engineers, IT and security teams, while translating technical trade-offs into clear business implications for executives and users. You know when to bring in a deeper technical expert.

- Strong ownership and builder energy. You have created structure or improved a process in an ambiguous, fast-moving environment and are motivated to build a company, not wait for clear directions.

- Excellent communication, stakeholder management and execution skills. You align teams without formal authority, surface risks early and drive decisions through to completion.

- Analytical and commercially minded: you can define meaningful success metrics, assess customer health, and are comfortable carrying renewal and NRR accountability.

- Fluent English; professional French strongly preferred (a significant share of our enterprise base is French-speaking).

Nice to have

- Experience with AI, machine learning, data platforms or complex enterprise software, including production deployments in regulated or security-sensitive environments.

- Experience working alongside deployment, engineering or professional services teams on custom use cases, and the transition from implementation to ongoing operation.

- Experience building adoption, change-management or customer education programs across large organizations.

- Experience at a forward-deployed, solutions-led company.

What We Offer

Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

title: Staff Software Engineer (Onboard Services)
description:
UFORCE exists to make aggression unaffordable.

Founded in Ukraine and headquartered in London, UFORCE is a defence-technology company with operations across Europe, the United States and Asia.

UFORCE builds uncrewed vessels, ground robotics and aircraft, autonomy software, and the command-and-control layer that operates them together. Each platform is deployable on its own, and stronger as part of the system. Its product lines include the MAGURA family of uncrewed surface vessels, the NEMESIS family of strike platforms, the LIUT family of ground robotic platforms, and counter-UAS systems.

About the role

The Staff Software Engineer (Onboard Services) will design, build, and operate the software services that run on UFORCE’s uncrewed vehicles — spanning video streaming, telemetry, autonomy integration, vehicle control, health monitoring, navigation, and device integrations.

You will turn independently evolved services into one secure, testable, and maintainable onboard platform. This is a hands-on software engineering role focused on production Python services, service architecture, messaging, and reliable operation on constrained Linux hardware, including Raspberry Pi, x86, and NVIDIA Jetson.

You will also own the boundary between the vehicle and the backend: clear, versioned contracts with cloud services, deployment systems, video infrastructure, and operator interfaces that work over intermittent, low-bandwidth links. Working with backend, autonomy, hardware, QA, and field teams, you will make releases predictable and catch failures on the bench, not in the field.

What you’ll do

- Define and evolve a unified onboard service architecture: service boundaries, messaging, configuration, startup ordering, readiness, watchdogs, and graceful degradation when dependencies or devices are unavailable.

- Build and migrate production services to shared patterns, using reusable libraries and a reference service template covering project structure, packaging, logging, health reporting, and lifecycle management.

- Standardise local service communication around NATS, with clear rules for integrating MAVLink, ZMQ IPC, and HTTP where appropriate.

- Design stable, versioned vehicle-to-backend contracts for telemetry, commands and acknowledgements, video metadata and control, configuration, health, and logs.

- Engineer for unreliable connectivity: buffering and store-and-forward, idempotent commands, explicit acknowledgements and timeouts, reconnection, back-off, and safe behaviour when the backend is unreachable.

- Implement secure-by-default services: least-privilege identities and messaging permissions, mutually authenticated and encrypted backend links, secure credential provisioning and rotation, sandboxed runtimes, and audit events for safety-critical commands.

- Strengthen automated testing across unit, contract, integration, simulation, and hardware-in-the-loop tests, with CI gates that catch regressions before release.

- Build safer release workflows with signed packages, dependency scanning, bench smoke and soak tests, staged fleet rollouts, and reliable rollback.

- Profile services and enforce practical CPU, memory, and latency budgets on target hardware.

- Improve field diagnostics through structured logs, metrics, standardised health reporting, post-mission log capture, and actionable runbooks.

- Document architectural decisions and service interfaces, communicate trade-offs clearly, and use AI coding tools to accelerate delivery without compromising quality.

What success looks like

- Actively developed onboard services converge on a shared architecture, supported Python runtime, messaging model, and service template.

- Engineers can take a new service from an empty repository to running on a bench vehicle in a day or less, with less duplicated infrastructure code.

- Vehicle-to-backend contracts remain compatible as cloud and vehicle software evolve at different speeds, preventing integration failures in the field.

- Authentication, least privilege, secret handling, runtime hardening, and supply-chain checks are consistently applied across the onboard stack.

- Automated tests and bench validation catch defects before deployment, reducing issues discovered in the field.

- Releases move predictably from bench validation to pilot vehicles and the wider fleet, with clear readiness gates and rollback procedures.

- Services stay within resource budgets and remain diagnosable under hardware constraints and degraded connectivity.

- Architecture documentation and runbooks help engineering, QA, and field teams integrate changes and resolve failures faster.

Required Qualifications

- 10+ years of professional experience in software engineering , delivering and operating production systems.

- 2+ years as a Tech Lead or Staff Engineer , owning architecture across multiple services or teams and establishing standards adopted by others.

- Expert Python — designs and ships production services (asyncio, packaging, testing, profiling, and performance); Node.js experience is a plus.

- Distributed / edge system architecture — has designed service architectures and messaging systems (e.g., NATS, MQTT, ZMQ, Kafka) with versioned contracts across system boundaries and unreliable networks.

- Web development and API experience — has built and evolved HTTP/WebSocket APIs and message-based integrations for multiple consumers.

- Security architecture — has led the design of authentication and authorisation, secrets and key management, secure updates, and supply-chain controls; security reviews or certification evidence are a strong plus.

- Quality engineering leadership — has established test strategies, CI gates, and staged release pipelines for a team or organisation; simulator or hardware-in-the-loop experience is a strong plus.

- Development with AI tools — uses AI coding assistants or agents daily and has introduced practices that help a team use them effectively and safely.

- C++, Rust, or Go experience is a plus.

- UxV, robotics, or embedded/edge Linux experience (e.g., MAVLink, GStreamer, serial/CAN devices, systemd services on constrained hardware) is a plus.

The nature of combat has changed.

Tomorrow’s battlefield success depends on autonomy, speed, and adaptability.

And UFORCE is ready.

title: Applied AI Engineer, Codex
description:
About the Team 

OpenAI’s Applied AI Engineering team helps organizations turn frontier AI capabilities into safe, reliable, and high-impact production systems. For software engineering organizations, this means helping customers adopt Codex and other OpenAI capabilities across the software development lifecycle—transforming how teams plan, build, test, review, and deliver software.

We work directly with engineering leaders and hands-on developers to identify high-value opportunities, design and implement AI-powered development workflows, and scale what works across engineering organizations. We turn lessons from these deployments into better products, reusable architectures, and technical patterns that help developers everywhere get more value from Codex.

About the Role 

As an Applied AI Engineer focused on Codex, you will partner directly with leading engineering organizations to design, build, and deploy AI systems that transform how software is developed. You will combine deep technical judgment, hands-on engineering, and customer leadership to take ambitious ideas from workflow and use-case selection through prototyping, evaluation, production rollout, and scaled adoption.

You will work alongside engineering teams to build advanced AI coding workflows, integrations, automations, and evaluation systems—often using Codex itself as part of your development process. You will help customers make technical decisions involving model behavior, agentic workflows, developer environments, security, reliability, evaluation, and operational readiness, while ensuring deployments translate into measurable improvements in engineering productivity and software delivery.

You will work closely with OpenAI Product, Research, Engineering, Security, Sales, and the broader Codex organization, translating real-world deployment experience into high-signal product and model feedback. Success is measured by production systems, sustained developer adoption, and meaningful improvements to how engineering organizations build software—not simply successful demonstrations or enablement activity.

This role is based in our London office. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will: 

- Partner directly with engineering leaders and hands-on developers to identify high-value opportunities for Codex and translate them into technical architectures, implementation plans, evaluation strategies, and measurable success criteria.

- Work hands-on in code to build prototypes, evaluation harnesses, reference implementations, integrations, workflow automations, and production accelerators—often using Codex as part of your own development process.

- Help customers progress from promising experiments to reliable production workflows, sustained developer adoption, and scaled impact across engineering organizations.

- Design systematic approaches for evaluating AI coding systems using representative software engineering tasks, automated graders, production signals, and developer feedback.

- Diagnose complex implementation challenges, reproduce failures, test hypotheses, and drive technical blockers toward resolution.

- Lead technical deep dives, workshops, and hands-on enablement that help engineering teams understand and adopt advanced AI coding workflows effectively and safely.

- Gather high-fidelity insights from real-world Codex deployments and translate them into clear product proposals, model feedback, and technical requirements for OpenAI Product, Research, and Engineering teams.

- Create reusable architectures, tooling, examples, guides, and technical patterns—including contributions to resources such as the OpenAI Cookbook—that accelerate future Codex deployments.

- Influence customer engineering strategy by helping technical leaders understand how AI coding systems can reshape their software development lifecycle, engineering practices, and organizational workflows.

You’ll thrive in this role if you: 

- Have a demonstrated track record of designing, building, and delivering software or AI systems in enterprise environments, including taking systems from prototype to production. Relevant backgrounds may include applied AI or ML engineering, forward-deployed engineering, software engineering, developer tooling, customer engineering, solutions architecture, or technical consulting.

- Can point to substantial personal contributions in code, architecture, evaluation, debugging, integrations, or production engineering—not only program, enablement, or stakeholder management.

- Are highly proficient in Python and comfortable working across modern software development environments; experience with JavaScript, TypeScript, or another relevant language is valuable.

- Are an active user of AI coding tools and have developed a strong point of view on how AI can improve developer productivity and software engineering workflows.

- Enjoy building high-signal prototypes, integrations, automations, and production solutions that demonstrate and deliver what AI coding systems can enable.

- Understand how to evaluate AI coding systems systematically, including designing representative tasks, automated evaluations, production signals, and mechanisms for incorporating developer feedback.

- Have navigated enterprise production requirements such as developer tooling integrations, reliability, observability, security, privacy, data governance, performance, and cost.

- Can connect technical decisions to developer workflows, adoption, engineering productivity, and measurable business outcomes.

- Communicate with clarity and credibility across hands-on engineers, engineering leaders, security teams, product leaders, and executives.

- Are comfortable leading technical workshops and hands-on sessions that help engineering organizations adopt new development workflows and technologies.

- Bring high agency, strong technical judgment, and end-to-end ownership in ambiguous and rapidly evolving environments.

- Learn quickly, challenge assumptions constructively, and collaborate with humility; deep prior experience with OpenAI products is not required.

title: Project Sceptrum - Multilingual AI Coding Evaluation Specialist - Dutch
description:
Join a short, paid project that tests whether AI coding agents work as well on instructions written in the target language as they do in English. Your language skills and technical background decide where you fit. 

About the project 

Welo Data is helping evaluate how well AI coding agents perform when the instructions they receive are written in languages other than English. Agents are given a real software engineering task in a code repository, and automated tests check whether they solved it. The code, repositories and tests stay exactly as they are. Only the human-written instructions change language, so the quality of every instruction directly affects the result. 

About the roles 

There are two roles on this project. We place you in one of them based on your experience & skillsets. 

- 
Translator: translate English software engineering task briefs into the target language. You keep every requirement, constraint and success condition, and you leave commands, file paths, API names, code and test conditions exactly as written in English. This role suits people with a stronger technical background, and translation experience is a plus. 

- 
Reviewer: compare each translation with the English source, check that nothing is missing, added or changed in meaning, correct errors, and log each correction by error type. This role suits people with strong translation, editing or review experience and enough technical familiarity to read code context. 

Who we are looking for 

- 
Native or near-native writing in the target language, and strong reading ability in English. 

- 
Either professional experience in translation, editing, review or technical writing, or a software background combined with excellent writing in the target language 

- 
Comfort reading technical text. Coding experience is a strong plus for the translation role and helpful for the review role. 

- 
Close attention to detail. In this project, a dropped clause can make a task fail. 

Project at a glance 

- 
Project duration: one week since the mid of November 

- 
Languages: Dutch

- 
Project time commitment: 6 hours per person 

- 
Project compensation: varies depends on different programming language 

- 
Work location: fully remote 

How selection works (major steps) 

- 
Screening questions: about 2 minutes. They cover your language background, translation and review experience, which programming languages you know and how well, and your availability. 

- 
Language test: short exercises in the target language. 

- 
Programming skills assessment: you will be invited to another opportunity, in the programming language you know best (Rust, Go, Python, or TypeScript / JavaScript). It confirms your technical level and places you in a language track. 

- 
Financial Onboarding & Role placement: complete the financial onboarding with Welo Data. In the meanwhile, you will be informed about the decision whether you are placed in the initial translation role or the review role. 

- 
Production: once you finish all steps above, our project team will contact you for production.

title: Tech Lead - Shared Backend Services
description:
Tech Lead - Shared Backend Services

Hybrid in London (UK) or Remote within the UK

We’re looking for a Tech Lead to join the Funnel Platform team. 

You’ll lead the team behind the shared services and frameworks that iwoca’s engineers build on. Those engineers are your customers, and the shared backend services feed iwoca’s lending decisions.

The company 

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

The Team 

Funnel Platform takes its name from iwoca’s customer funnel – a business’s journey from first application to repeat lending. It owns the shared services and frameworks that the customer journey teams along that funnel build on, in the UK and Germany. The team’s aim is to make those services reliable, and simple for other teams to change.

The team works across three areas:

- Credit data. Looking after the services that bring in data from the UK credit bureaus and Companies House.

- Bank data. Looking after the service other teams use to work with business bank transactions.

- New shared services. Building services that several teams need, including one for split tests.

The team is small – three backend engineers, including you. Infrastructure, such as Kubernetes and cloud hosting, sits with a separate team, so the work here is software.

The Role 

As the Tech Lead in Funnel Platform, you’ll stay hands-on in the code while you lead the team. The team has no product manager, so you’ll decide what it builds, with input on priorities from the leaders of iwoca’s customer journey teams. You’ll report to the head of engineering for the customer journey teams.

- Ownership. You’ll be accountable for the team’s existing services and the new ones it builds, from design to production.

- Engineering standards. You’ll shape how the team designs and tests the shared services, and review the changes other teams make to them.

- Impact. You’ll improve the services iwoca’s customer journey teams depend on, so your work speeds up theirs.

- Influence. You’ll use data to persuade the customer journey teams and their leaders to back shared-service work that helps all of them.

- Leadership and growth. You’ll line-manage the team’s two engineers, and give them the guidance and context to lead projects of their own.

The requirements 

Essential:

- Technical leadership. You’ve led engineers as a tech lead for around two years, while staying hands-on in the code.

- Shared services. You’ve built and run backend services or frameworks that other engineering teams use and contribute to. You’ve reviewed their changes and shaped how they use your work.

- Backend engineering. You know at least one backend language in depth, and you’ve designed and run distributed systems in production.

- Problem finding. You’ve set a team’s priorities without a product manager, talking to the people who use your work to find the real problem before you design a fix. You can show what a technical trade-off costs or saves the business.

- AI leverage. You’ve used AI to produce work you couldn’t have delivered without it – such as an internal tool or a migration. You know where it helps keep shared code easy to maintain, and you review what it produces before it goes live.

Bonus:

- Python and Django. You’ve built production services in Python with Django.

- Numerical background. You’re comfortable analysing data and drawing conclusions you can defend.

- Experimentation. You’ve built tools that other teams use to run split tests.

- Fintech. You’ve worked at a fintech or another financial services business.

The salary 

We expect to pay from £100,000 to £130,000 for this role. But, we’re open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.

The culture 

At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective.

We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better. We provide the infrastructure where every iwocan always has access to the best models and where those models have access to all of our data. We will help our people to learn how to use and grow with the new tools available to them.

The offices 

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

- Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

- Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits 

- Flexible working hours.

- Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.

- A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.

- 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.

- A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.

- Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.

- 3% Pension contributions on total earnings.

- An employee equity incentive scheme.

- Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.

- Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme.

- Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:

- A learning and development budget for everyone.

- Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers.

- Access to learning platforms like Treehouse.

Ideally, you have hands-on experience in AI use case conceptualization or data platform tracking.

- Business & analytical mindset: You combine strong analytical skills with a business-oriented perspective. You enjoy identifying business problems and translating them into practical AI and data-driven solutions.

More importantly, you know how to leverage AI tools - from LLM environments to agentic workflows - to run analysis, generate insights, and accelerate delivery. Experience with SQL, BI tools, or programming languages is not a requirement, but comfort with structured data and a hands-on attitude toward new tools is expected.

- Communication & collaboration: You communicate complex technical topics clearly in both German and English. You enjoy working in interdisciplinary teams and collaborating across different levels and functions (e.g., translating requirements between business stakeholders and data scientists).

- Personal attributes: You are proactive, structured, and solution-oriented, with a strong client focus and stakeholder understanding. You thrive in dynamic environments and enjoy solving complex problems.

- Languages: Business-fluent German and English are required - you will participate in client workshops, present to senior stakeholders, and write deliverables in both languages. Additional languages are a plus.

- Work Eligibility: A valid work permit for Germany.

Why ARTEFACT? 

- Impactful client work: Work on challenging projects with leading national and international clients across data, digitalisation, and advanced data strategy.

- Career growth opportunities: We believe in performance over tenure. Your growth is driven by your impact, not your length of service, with clear opportunities to progress and diverse career prospects.

- Learning & development: Join a team of passionate Data Consultants who actively support each other. You'll learn through diverse projects, collaboration, and exposure to leading experts in the field - including international work.

title: Agentic Systems Engineer (Digital Services)
description:
Overview 

We're looking for an Agentic Systems Engineer, to work on systems that haven't existed before. Think of an Agentic Coach that navigates the unpredictability of human biology, or the software architecture behind a fully automated Dark Lab. These aren't chatbots waiting for questions. They're proactive systems that maintain world models, interpret human intent, and intervene before the user knows to ask. These systems create genuine impact for clients tackling complex problems at the forefront of technology.

Building them means designing and wiring agent harnesses: layered architectures that span from sensor-edge reasoning to high-level planning, backed by stateful multi-turn reasoning, persistent per-user memory, and robust evaluation pipelines.

You'll work in two directions at once. Internally, you'll use the latest AI tools to sharpen how we build, prototype, and ship. Externally, you'll deliver the breakthrough systems our clients deploy, designed to move from prototype to production at pace.

There's no single technology stack. You'll work with agents, multi-agent systems, and the latest generative AI tools, but your work will always be grounded in solid software engineering. Expect to build scalable distributed systems in core languages like Python and TypeScript, leveraging frameworks such as NextJS and Pydantic, agent orchestration tools (LangGraph, CrewAI), and protocols like MCP. You'll deploy on cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, Azure) using Docker, Kubernetes, and infrastructure-as-code, backed by rigorous CI/CD and observability (OpenTelemetry, Prometheus).

Due to the clients we work with, you must be eligible for UK security clearance.

What you'll be doing: 

- AI System Architecture: Designing and implementing the logic for autonomous systems, including maintaining world models, integrating multimodal sensing, and building real-time human-machine interaction loops.

- Infrastructure & Production Engineering: Designing the underlying software for scalable, secure, and observable cloud deployments. You will apply the engineering rigor required to take experimental AI from concept to robust live launch.

- Rapid Client Prototyping: Driving a demo-first delivery model. You will focus on fast experimentation to actively show tangible value and working software to clients, while maintaining the engineering standards required for production deployment.

- Domain Translation & Integration: Partnering directly with deep-tech subject matter experts (like biologists and roboticists) to apply software solutions to complex physical constraints.

- Agent Evaluation & Optimisation: Developing frameworks to measure, monitor and improve agent performance. You will design evaluation strategies, identify failure modes, and apply systematic testing to ensure agents are reliable, predictable and effective in real-world environments.

What you need to succeed: 

- Applied AI Expertise: You have hands-on experience building LLM-based agentic systems, with a solid grasp of the fundamentals: planning, reasoning, tool use, memory and orchestration. You know how to evaluate and monitor agents so you can measure how they perform in production.

- Core Software Fluency: You possess strong programming skills, good testing and deployment practices, and practical experience in cloud engineering, containerisation, and modern DevOps. You can design scalable, resilient systems, and you know that great agents still require excellent software engineering foundations.

- Navigating Ambiguity: You are comfortable working with uncertainty and evolving requirements. You break complex, ill-defined problems into clear, logical steps. You recognise that requirements evolve as new information emerges and can make sound engineering judgements about when rapid experimentation is appropriate and when a more rigorous approach is required.

- Communication: You communicate complex technical concepts clearly and confidently, adapting your style to different audiences. You are comfortable engaging with clients, engineers, scientists and business leaders, ensuring technical insights translate into meaningful decisions and outcomes.

- Collaboration and Influence: You know how to challenge constructively, influence through evidence and insight, and help others navigate trade-offs in fast-moving environments.

- Problem Solving: You enjoy tackling complex technical challenges and can quickly distil ambiguity into actionable plans. You combine analytical thinking with pragmatism to identify the right solution and move projects forward.

Some projects at Cambridge Consultants are subject to security restrictions. This role requires you to obtain a Security Check (SC) level security clearance ( United Kingdom Security Vetting: Applicant ). You must be able to work in the UK without restrictions in accordance with UK National Law and be prepared to successfully undertake an appropriate level of UK National Security Vetting according to UK Government National Security Vetting criteria. Please be aware that, for roles requiring Security Check clearance, applicants will typically need to have been continuously resident in the UK for a minimum of 5 years immediately prior to applying for this role in order to meet the requirements for Security Check (SC) clearance.

What we offer: 

- 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays (with the option to buy 10 more a year)

- Company bonus (profit share)

- Flexible working patterns and hybrid working

- Medical insurance and group income protection

- Employee assistance programme and mental health support group

- Enhanced maternity/paternity leave

- Sabbatical leave

- Travel insurance (business and leisure)

- Generous company pension plan

- Personalised career development and training plans

- Free breakfast and two-course lunch in the office every day

- Free onsite parking and we are close to public transport links

- A variety of events organised by our social committee, ranging from summer and Christmas parties to board game nights and socials at our own rooftop bar!

Why Cambridge Consultants? 

At Cambridge Consultants, you'll contribute to radical, new-to-the-world innovation that transforms business, society and the planet. Joining our multidisciplinary teams means helping to turn bold ideas into reality, harnessing the power of deep tech to create products, services and experiences that have never existed before. Whether you're advancing technologies, shaping strategy, supporting operations or driving commercial growth, it's an opportunity to make a real impact and help create the future.

title: Research Engineer

Genomics aims to help people live longer, healthier lives in two ways: super-charging drug discovery and development for novel treatments with our AI-enabled advanced genetic analytics platform, and by helping people understand their personal risk of common chronic diseases through polygenic risk scores - giving doctors and health systems the chance to get the right people into the right prevention, screening and treatment programmes at the right time.

title: Senior Robotics Engineer
description:
About Inbolt

Deploying an industrial robot still takes months of integration and programming, and the moment a part, a process, or a position changes, it starts over. Inbolt makes it take minutes.

Our generalist vision model gives robots the ability to see, think, and adapt in real time, so any robot can master any process, part, or station. Set up from a CAD model in minutes and compatible with FANUC, ABB, KUKA, Yaskawa, Comau, and Universal Robots, Inbolt runs in production at Stellantis, Toyota, Ford, GM, Bosch, and more, with 200+ systems live across 100+ factories on three continents.

We're a team based in Paris, Detroit, and Japan, and we're growing fast. Here's the role:

This position is Paris, France based. 

Role Overview

Your mission is to own the integration of complex robotics features into Inbolt Studio, at 100% industrial-grade quality, from architecture to production on the factory floor.

As Senior Robotics Engineer, you are the technical reference for robot control and robot programming in our product. Our roadmap covers static and dynamic robot control whatever the brand. You will architect and build these capabilities, integrate them end to end into Inbolt Studio, and make sure they run reliably on real robots in demanding production environments.

You will work at the intersection of robotics, 3D perception, and software engineering, in a small fast growing team where your contribution is visible and your decisions shape the product. This is not an R&D position: your work has a daily impact on what runs in production at Inbolt customers.

Want to take your robotics career to the next level by building the future of robot vision guidance in the real world? This role is for you.

Responsibilities

Feature ownership and architecture

- Own the design and integration of complex robotics features into Inbolt Studio, from architecture to production release

- Deliver the roadmap on static and dynamic robot control

- Make the key technical decisions on motion planning, robot control, and real-time constraints, and defend them with data

- Push the limits of the current codebase and propose better architectures when needed

Industrial-grade quality

- Guarantee industrial-grade quality: every feature is tested, validated on real robots, robust to edge cases, and safe to run in a factory

- Set the standards for code quality, testing, and review in the robotics team, and keep the PR process efficient

- Own the quality of your deliverables: code, engineering reports, and validation results

- Estimate lead times fairly for Epics, deliver on schedule, and flag early when a plan is drifting

From lab idea to production

- Turn prototypes into production features, validated in real factory conditions at customer sites

- Integrate and validate Inbolt’s solution across industrial robot brands and their programming environments

- Keep a solid view of the state of the art in robotics, and bring what is relevant into the product

Technical leadership and collaboration

- Act as the technical reference for the application engineering (RAE) and sales teams on complex customer cases, feasibility, and escalations

- Review designs and code, mentor engineers, and take part in interviews for new hires

- Work closely with the Lead Robotics engineer, other engineering teams, and deployment teams in Paris, the US, and Japan

Profile

Inbolt values end-to-end ownership, high rigor, and a hands-on curiosity. We move fast while staying precise, with a proactive, autonomous, results-driven mindset and strong collaboration with engineering teams.

Required Skills

- 5+ years of strong professional experience in robotics, in a startup or a large company, with a track record of owning complex features end to end

- Strong expertise in robotics motion planning: trajectory generation, path planning, collision avoidance, and motion optimization for industrial robot arms

- Strong expertise in real-time robot control, both static and dynamic (sensor-driven): closed-loop control, low-latency sensor-to-motion pipelines, and deterministic, performance-critical code running on real robots

- Excellence in software development: strong Python and/or C++, solid engineering practices (testing, code review, version control, CI/CD)

- Proven record of shipping complex robotics features to production at industrial-grade quality: reliability, test strategy, and validation on real robots

- Ability to design abstractions that work across robot brands and programming languages

- Solid foundations in robotics: kinematics, frames and transformations, and integration with industrial or collaborative robot arms

- Technical leadership: you make architecture decisions, raise the bar in code reviews, and mentor other engineers

- Appetite for fast development and visible impact: you iterate quickly, ship often, and take ownership of the result

- Clear communicator, able to explain technical topics to engineers, sales, and customers

- Fluent in English; French is a big plus given daily interactions with the Paris team

Additional Plus

- A PhD in robotics or a related field is appreciated, as long as your focus is on shipping: this role is about production impact, not research

- Experience with 3D vision, point clouds, computer vision, or machine learning applied to perception

- Experience with industrial robot brands (Universal Robots, ABB, FANUC, KUKA, Yaskawa, Comau) and their programming languages

- Experience with ROS or other robotics frameworks

- Experience deploying or supporting systems on customer sites in industrial environments

- Experience as a tech lead or team lead of a robotics team

Position details

- Role: Senior Robotics Engineer

- Team: Engineering

- Location: Paris, France, in our office at 12 rue Vivienne, 75002 Paris

- Start date: ASAP

- Employment type: Full-time

- Collaboration: you will work closely with teams in Paris, the US, and Japan, and your work will directly impact deployments in factories worldwide

Why join Inbolt 

- Real impact, on real factory floors: your work runs in production at Stellantis, Toyota, Ford, GM, and Bosch, across 100+ factories on three continents.

- Ownership from day one: we value end-to-end ownership, high rigor, and hands-on curiosity, and we move fast while staying precise.

- An international team: Paris, Detroit, and Japan, working closely with world-class robotics and automation partners.

- A seat at the start of something big: we're building the default intelligence layer for every industrial robot, on every brand.

Benefits 

We're building our benefits location by location, so they fit local needs and practices in each country where we operate.

- 📍 Prime office locations in Paris and Detroit

- 🤝 Team-building events & off-sites

- 🐶 Bring-your-dog-to-work policy

- 🍽️ Lunch expenses covered

- ✈️ Customer site visits in real factories

- and more…

Benefits may vary by location and contract type.

Our hiring process 

- Introduction call (30 min) with our Talent team, to get to know you and answer your questions.

- Interview with your future manager, including a case study or technical exercise depending on the role.

- Meet the team: a conversation with the people you will work with every day.

- Final round with our founders.

- Reference checks.

The exact steps can vary slightly by role. We keep the process short and transparent, and we'll keep you posted at every step.

Ready to give robots sight? 

Inbolt is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applications from everyone, whatever their background, and a real person reads every application. Even if you don't tick every box, if this role excites you, we'd love to hear from you.

Required Qualifications

• Demonstrated operational ownership: observability, on-call readiness, incident response, and production debugging.

Nice to have

• Experience with distributed systems reliability patterns (idempotency, retries, transactional workflows, consistency trade-offs).

About The Role

We're looking for a software engineer to own the architecture, data handling, and product layer of the software stack at one of Valinor’s product companies, currently in stealth. The system turns raw sensor data into a usable, trusted picture for the end user. You'll work directly with the General Manager and alongside a small team of engineers to rapidly develop a new product. You’ll also partner with product enablement at the Valinor Hub to stand up infrastructure and management.

We see this as a step-up role: someone who has already been part of building a system like this, whether embedded/edge software, sensor or data pipelines, or detection and classification work, as a strong contributor, and is ready to own that kind of architecture for the first time, with direct partnership from the GM on the highest-stakes tradeoffs.

What You'll Do

1. Overall Software Architecture 

- 
Design the software architecture that ties the products data flow, processing, and user-facing product together end to end.

- 
Define clean interfaces with the sensor integration and API work, so the pieces fit into a coherent whole rather than a collection of one-offs.

- 
Make and document the core architecture decisions early, since the system needs to flex as we learn what the product needs to become.

2. Data Handling & Pipeline 

- 
Architect the edge vs. cloud processing split — what runs on-system under power/compute constraints versus what gets backhauled.

- 
Stand up time-series and object storage systems for sensor and telemetry data, and the ingestion pipeline that gets data from the system to backend reliable.

- 
Design for bandwidth-constrained, compression-aware data transport, and build in the data versioning and observability needed to trust what's flowing in as sensor types multiply.

3. Detection, Classification & Pattern-of-life 

- 
Work with various sensor modalities, including acoustic, EO/IR, radar, RF/AIS, and others, to build detection and classification capability — starting with classical signal-processing methods where appropriate, and applied ML where it earns its complexity.

- 
Contribute to pattern-of-life anomaly detection work.

- 
Fuse multi-modal signals into a single detection/classification output.

4. User Interface — Configuration & Visualization 

- 
Build the product configuration interface and the geospatial data visualization layer (the common operating picture) the end customer will actually use.

What We're Looking For

Required 

- 
Architecture contribution, ready to lead: you've been part of a small team that designed and built a system with real architectural stakes — edge/embedded software, sensor or data pipelines, or similar — and you're ready to own that kind of system yourself for the first time.

- 
Data pipeline and storage experience: comfortable designing and operating time-series data systems and message-based ingestion pipelines (MQTT, Kafka, or equivalent), including handling for intermittent/unreliable connectivity.

- 
Full-stack range: comfortable moving between backend/data pipeline work (Python, Go, or similar) and frontend (React/TypeScript) without needing a specialist for each; enough familiarity with embedded/edge constraints to architect around them, even if you're not writing firmware yourself.

- 
At least one sensing/signal domain: hands-on experience with at least one of acoustic, EO/IR, or radar signal processing or detection — and genuine excitement to pick up the others as the product grows into them.

- 
Cloud infrastructure ownership: able to stand up and maintain CI/CD and cloud infrastructure (AWS preferred; GovCloud experience a plus) without a dedicated DevOps function yet in place.

- 
Step-up temperament: proven ability to build and rebuild quickly with loose specs, and comfort taking ownership of a decision you'd previously have brought to someone else.

Strongly Preferred 

- 
TAK (or similar government system) integration experience: hands-on work integrating with TAK (ATAK/WinTAK/TAK Server) or a comparable government C2/situational-awareness system is a significant plus.

- 
Applied ML experience, particularly anomaly detection or pattern-of-life modeling.

- 
Prior experience in defense or dual-use tech, including familiarity with the general shape of DoD software requirements (security, data handling, eventual ATO/RMF processes).

- 
Geospatial visualization experience (Mapbox, Cesium, deck.gl , or similar).

- 
Prior experience on an autonomous systems, robotics, or maritime/subsea platform.

What Valinor Offers

- 
Competitive salary, equity packages, and benefits, including health, dental, and vision insurance - fully covered for employees, 401K, development stipends, among others.

- 
Unlimited PTO and two-week company holiday at the end of every calendar year.

- 
We are a pro-mental health and pro-family company - we actually encourage employees to spend time with themselves and their families. Valinor also provides fertility benefits to those just beginning that journey.

- 
Fun work environment - we like to laugh and take care of each other, but we also deeply respect the mission in front of us.

This role requires the candidate be eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance. Active clearance preferred, but not required.

title: Senior Data Engineer
description:
We're the world's leading consumer healthcare platform, supporting millions of patients across the US, Australia, the UK, Germany, Japan, Spain and Canada.

We're driven by the belief that good health should last a lifetime, and that to get there we need to deliver the personalised, high quality and empathetic care that the traditional system cannot support.

You'll partner with our care teams of prescribers, nurses, health coaches, pharmacists and dietitians to support patients across preventative health, weight management and specific women's and men's health conditions.

We joined Hims & Hers so that you can do all of the above on a bigger scale, with more ambition, a stronger global brand and the resources to deliver care to patients in dozens of countries.

We're looking for people who appreciate and are excited by the enormity and uniqueness of this challenge, and want to work in the most ambitious, smart, fast moving and positive sum environment of their lives to transform how healthcare is delivered globally.

We hope that's you.

About the Role

As a Senior Data Engineer, you will help design, build and look after the data pipelines and infrastructure that support insight, experimentation and machine learning across our business. Based in our London HQ, you will support the Hims US business as part of the wider Hims & Hers data community, working together with data teams on both sides of the Atlantic.

Working across data engineering, analytics and platform engineering, you will collaborate with analytics engineers, data analysts, machine learning engineers and business colleagues to turn raw data into reliable, trusted and easy-to-use data products. You will care deeply about quality, reliability and performance as we grow our preventative care ecosystem globally.

What You’ll Do

- Build Scalable Pipelines: Design and build data pipelines that are dependable, high quality and ready to grow with the business.

- Care for Containerised Deployments: Take responsibility for production deployments of containerised data applications and ETL infrastructure on Kubernetes (EKS) across our AWS and GCP environments.

- Support Data Processing & Integration: Build and look after batch and streaming workflows using Python, SQL, dbt, Kafka (AWS MSK), Flink and Airflow, bringing data into the BigQuery warehouse via CDC and user event tracking (UET) streams and REST APIs.

- Improve Quality & Reliability: Implement testing frameworks, monitoring as code (Datadog or equivalent), anomaly detection, SLOs and runbooks so our data stays trustworthy and dependable.

- Enable Self-Service Onboarding: Build platform capabilities such as config-driven table onboarding that help analytics engineers, analysts and business colleagues bring new data onto the platform without bespoke engineering.

- Partner Across Data Teams: Work with analytics engineers to keep core data sources performant and dependable, and support ML engineers with reliable platform foundations for deploying models. Transformation logic and data marts remain with Analytics Engineering.

- Share Engineering Practices: Work with the wider Data Platform team to agree on and uphold good engineering practices.

- Embed Governance & Security: Partner with legal and security colleagues on governance, data compliance and security policies, including HIPAA/PHI handling, UK GDPR and cross-border access to patient data.

- Deliver Infrastructure as Code: Help shape how we approach DevOps on Terraform (IaC) and CI/CD within the data platform, taking responsibility for versioning and deployment of data pipelines.

About You 

- Data Engineering Depth: You are an experienced data engineer (typically 5+ years) who can design and look after pipelines end to end, from ingestion through to consumption. You are comfortable working with Python, SQL, dbt, Kafka, Flink, Airflow and REST APIs.

- Infrastructure & Operational Skills: You have experience running containerised infrastructure on Kubernetes and are comfortable with Terraform, CI/CD and code versioning practices for data workloads, ideally across both AWS and GCP.

- Quality & Reliability Mindset: You care about data quality as a core part of the job, with hands-on experience implementing testing frameworks, observability tooling, SLOs and runbooks.

- Enablement Focus: You care about the people using your data. You have a track record of building platform tooling that helps analysts, analytics engineers and colleagues feel confident working with data themselves.

- Cross-Functional Collaboration: You work well with analytics engineers, machine learning engineers, DevOps, legal and security, and can explain technical trade-offs clearly to non-technical colleagues.

- Responsibility & Judgement: You take responsibility for the systems you build, help the team grow through code review and mentoring, and make thoughtful calls in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.

Nice to have 

- Experience in regulated sectors (such as healthtech, fintech or gaming), finding creative paths forward inside compliance constraints rather than being stopped by them. Familiarity with reverse-ETL / data activation tools such as Hightouch or Segment is also a plus.

Why join Eucalyptus

- What's next - Our goal for the next three years is to support 1 million patients globally to live better for longer, launching into new conditions, demographics and geographies.

- Build something world-changing - We're on the path to becoming the world's largest international digital healthcare company. It will be challenging, fast-paced and deeply rewarding.

- Make real impact - Your work directly shapes patient outcomes and scales evidence-based care across markets.

- Accelerate your growth - High ownership, continuous feedback and dedicated development support.

- Join a motivated team - Talented peers solving complex clinical and operational problems at scale.

What's ahead in the UK

- Be an owner - Your own stake in the business with our employee options programme

- Invest in your growth - Annual development budget plus 3 days of professional development leave

- Work flexibly - Hybrid setup with 3 days a week in our Old Street office, designed for focus and collaboration

- Support your well-being - Private health insurance through Vitality, or a monthly wellness allowance to spend on what matters most to you

- Take time off - 25 days of holiday, enhanced parental leave and work from anywhere 3 weeks a year

- Join a connected team - A vibrant office culture with regular socials, clubs, after-school sport and seasonal events

At Eucalyptus, we value individuals from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives, and we embrace the unique qualities each person brings. title: Sr. Data Engineer
description:
Headquarters: Remote

About Carrot: 

Carrot is the leading global fertility and family care platform, built on intelligent care orchestration: the right clinical guidance, at the right moment, in the context of each member’s life. More than a thousand multinational employers, health plans, and health systems trust Carrot to support millions of members across 195 countries – from pre-pregnancy through menopause and major life moments in between. Carrot's comprehensive clinical program delivers industry-leading cost savings for plan sponsors and award-winning experiences and improved outcomes for millions of people worldwide.

Carrot is widely regarded as a defining force in healthcare innovation as a recipient of several top-tier awards, including Fast Company's 'Most Innovative Companies' and CNBC's '100 Barrier Breaking Startups'. The company is regularly cited by leading global outlets — including The Economist, Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal, NPR, ABC News, and Harvard Business Review — as a leading voice on digital health, the future of work, and family health. Learn more at get-carrot.com .

The Opportunity 

Carrot is seeking a Sr. Data Engineer to lead the evolution, reliability, and scalability of our modern data infrastructure across analytics, reporting, and business intelligence. In this role, you will architect, build, and maintain robust, automated data pipelines, orchestrate workflows, integrate diverse data sources, and partner with stakeholders across the business to deliver secure, compliant, high-quality data solutions.

Your work will span the full data lifecycle, from architecting resilient ETL/ELT pipelines and developing real-time and batch data integrations to automating reporting, reducing technical debt, and enabling advanced analytics. Sr. Data Engineers at Carrot are operational stewards and technical mentors, driving improvements in system maturity, cost efficiency, automation, and collaborative practices.

You will join our Data Engineering team, which develops and optimizes scalable data pipelines and cloud infrastructure to enable secure, automated reporting and analytics across Carrot. The team collaborates closely with Business Intelligence, Product, Finance, Legal, and Commercial partners to deliver reliable integrations and self-serve solutions that drive business insights and operational efficiency.

What You’ll Own 

In this role, you will:

- Architect, build, test, deploy, and maintain scalable, automated ETL/ELT pipelines using Python, dbt, and orchestration tools such as Prefect and Airflow

- Administer and optimize cloud-based data warehouse and lake platforms, including Snowflake, AWS (S3, Redshift), and Google Cloud, integrating new sources and tuning for performance and cost

- Orchestrate data workflows with custom scheduling, alerting, dependency management, monitoring, and error resolution

- Design and maintain secure external data flows through SFTP, Files.com, and APIs, with a focus on reliability and compliance

- Automate manual reporting and operational tasks, building robust, reusable pipeline components that reduce operational overhead

- Partner with backend product engineers to optimize production database schemas with analytics use cases in mind

- Strengthen data quality, lineage, governance, and documentation practices across key data domains

- Mentor teammates and reinforce best practices in version control, code review, and structured workflow management

What Success Looks Like 

In your first 12–18 months, you will have:

- Taken end-to-end ownership of core pipelines and integrations, with measurable improvements in reliability, data recency, and cost efficiency

- Automated high-effort manual workflows, reducing operational risk and freeing capacity for higher-value engineering work

- Delivered secure, compliant data integrations that stakeholders across the business trust for decision-making

- Strengthened observability across the platform, including monitoring, alerting, and incident response for critical data workflows

- Established yourself as a technical mentor and a go-to partner for Business Intelligence, Product, and cross-functional teams

About You 

You likely have:

- Expert-level proficiency in Snowflake, dbt, and Python for data modeling, transformation, pipeline development, and advanced analytics

- Advanced SQL skills for complex querying, large-scale data model design, and database optimization

- Proven experience architecting, building, testing, deploying, and maintaining scalable, automated ETL/ELT pipelines using modern orchestration tools such as Prefect and Airflow

- Hands-on administration of cloud-based data warehouse and lake platforms, including Snowflake, AWS (S3, Redshift), and Google Cloud

- A strong understanding of secure external data flows through SFTP, Files.com, and APIs, with a focus on reliability and compliance

- Mastery of version control (Git, GitHub) and structured workflow management (Jira) for code review, audit trails, and operational transparency

- A demonstrated ability to automate and simplify complex manual tasks, building robust, reusable pipeline components

- Dependability, adaptability, and a collaborative approach to engineering, thriving in dynamic and ambiguous environments

Nice to Have ⭐ 

While not required, we would be especially excited if you bring:

- Hands-on experience in startup or rapid-growth environments, delivering technical solutions under shifting priorities

- A background supporting business intelligence, analytics, and data science teams through large-scale integrations and multi-tenant reporting

- Familiarity with both batch and event-driven ingestion paradigms, including near-real-time pipelines built on Snowflake, dbt, and Python

- Experience automating operational, financial, or compliance-driven workflows within cloud data environments

- Exposure to audit, privacy, and compliance frameworks such as SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR, ISO, and SOX, particularly in data governance and secure access controls

- Experience in regulated industries such as healthcare, healthtech, or SaaS

Why This Role Matters 

Reliable data is the foundation of how Carrot operates, from the analytics that guide business decisions to the reporting our customers and partners depend on. The systems this role owns determine the accuracy, recency, and security of data used across the entire company.

As Carrot scales globally, the Sr. Data Engineer will make our data platform more automated, resilient, and cost-efficient, enabling teams across the business to move faster with data they trust. This work directly supports Carrot's mission of expanding access to fertility and family-building care worldwide.

Interview Process 

We believe in a thoughtful and transparent interview process designed to create alignment for both candidates and our team.

For this role, candidates can expect:

- Recruiter Screen — 30 minutes

- Hiring Manager Interview — 30–45 minutes

- Cross-Functional Panel Interviews — 45 minutes

- Executive Leadership Conversation — 30 minutes

- Hiring Manager Wrap-Up — 15 minutes

Throughout the process, we will share additional context about the team, business priorities, customer landscape, and what success looks like in this role.

Why Candidates Join Carrot 

Carrot offers the opportunity to do meaningful work in service of a deeply human mission.

Highlights include:

- A mission-driven company focused on expanding access to fertility and family-forming care globally.

- A high-growth environment where leaders are empowered to shape strategy and drive impact.

- Competitive compensation, equity, and comprehensive benefits.

- Flexible Time Off and a culture that actively encourages employees to recharge.

- Comprehensive parental leave and family-forming benefits.

- A collaborative, inclusive, and values-driven culture.

- The opportunity to work alongside passionate, thoughtful teammates committed to improving healthcare outcomes worldwide.

Compensation:

title: Data Engineer: Merchant Intelligence Agent

About the Team

We are transforming how digital merchandising teams work: instead of digging through reports and configuring rules by hand, they ask in plain language, get answers grounded in their own data, and approve the changes the agent prepares. Customers already rely on the agent to save time and make better decisions.

We own the agent end to end, from the first question a merchant asks to the answer they act on. We also own the analytics behind it: the pipelines and cubes for search, browse, and recommendation performance, and the metric definitions merchants rely on.

That is why we build the agent and the Customer Dashboard as a platform that every Constructor team extends. We create the foundation that other teams build on: the agent framework, shared components, and infrastructure. On top of it, teams add their own data, tools, and skills, so the agent can answer questions in their domain and the dashboard can show their features without separate interfaces. Each new capability gives merchants more ways to grow their business.

- Build and own the batch pipelines and cubes behind dashboard analytics and agent insights

- Shape data for each role: a merchandiser's category, a product manager's funnel step, an executive's total

- Own data quality and trust: freshness, monitoring, alerting, and metric definitions

- Work with engineers, analysts, and product to find the data the agent is missing and turn merchant questions into data products

- Ship your data into the product: simple analytics UIs, and the agent skills, tools, and prompts that use it

Must-have 

- Proficiency in Python and SQL (any dialect)

- Experience building and maintaining batch data pipelines with Spark (PySpark)

- Familiarity with the big data stack: Databricks, ClickHouse and dbt

- Experience with data modeling for analytics: aggregated tables and cubes that feed dashboards and APIs

- Experience with data quality and pipeline monitoring: freshness checks, alerting, incident response

- Ability to prototype fast and pick the metrics that matter in e-commerce

- Ability to translate business questions into technical requirements, and back

- Clear communication with engineers and non-technical stakeholders

Nice-to-have 

- Experience building frontend UIs, or willingness to work across the full stack to ship data into product features

- Experience with pandas, NumPy

- Experience building AI agents: tools, skills, prompts, context, and evaluations

- Experience with real-time analytics: ClickHouse, Cube.js

- Experience with AWS

- Familiarity with statistics for experimentation (A/B tests)

Benefits

title: AI Applied Scientist
description:
About the Science and AI Team 

The Science and AI team is at the heart of Maki People. It builds the science and AI behind our platform, from job analysis and assessments to AI interviews and predicting performance. Led by our Head of Science, Aiden Loe, and working closely with our COO, Paul-Louis Caylar, the team brings together business psychologists, psychometricians and AI scientists. Together, they make sure every hiring decision on our platform is accurate, consistent and fair. 

As Maki grows, the Science and AI team’s job is to show, with evidence, that our approach leads to better hiring decisions.

About the Role 

The AI Applied Scientist turns our science into results for clients. Most of your time goes on client projects: adapting our AI scoring to each client’s roles, analysing their data, and showing them what it means. The rest goes on improving the scoring systems that every client relies on.

1. Client projects 

- Adapt AI scoring for structured interviews, job-specific skills and multilingual proficiency to each client’s roles and needs.

- Analyse client assessment and performance data to show how scores relate to job performance and retention.

- Set and review cut-offs and thresholds with clients, backed by evidence.

- Present findings and recommendations directly to clients, in a way non-technical audiences can act on.

- Work closely with implementation and customer success teams from setup to go-live.

2. Testing scoring quality 

- Compare AI scores with expert ratings to check accuracy and reliability before anything goes live.

- Test robustness to prompt variation, input noise and adversarial behaviour such as prompt injection.

3. Fairness in practice 

- Run bias checks across demographic groups for each client project.

- Apply mitigation techniques such as reweighting and calibration without losing model performance.

- Support fairness reports and compliance documentation for clients.

4. Improving our scoring systems 

- Help choose the right models and prompts for production, balancing accuracy, speed and cost.

- Support the move onto self-hosted open-weight models, including fine-tuning on expert-rated data.

- Work with engineering to roll out scoring changes safely.

As one of Maki People’s early employees, you’ll help shape the team’s future.

Our Ideal Candidate 

Required

- MSc or PhD in data science, machine learning, psychology or a related field, or equivalent industry experience.

- Hands-on experience with LLM-based scoring or evaluation.

- Strong Python or R skills, with solid statistical analysis.

- Experience presenting data-driven findings to clients or senior business stakeholders.

- Able to manage several projects at once and keep to deadlines.

Preferred

- Experience in consulting, people analytics or assessment.

- Working knowledge of psychometric concepts such as reliability, validity and IRT.

- Experience testing AI systems for fairness and bias.

- Experience fine-tuning language models, for example with LoRA.

- Working knowledge of ethical AI and compliance, such as the EU AI Act.

Application Process 

- Stage 1 - Screening assessment (25 min)

- Stage 2 - Power skill assessment with our AI agent (15 min)

- Stage 3 - Hiring manager interview (45 min)

- Stage 4 - Executive interview (45 min)

- Stage 5 - Deep-dive technical interview (60 min)

- Stage 6 - Interview with Co-founder (30 min)

description:
AI/ML Engineer — Generative AI Mission Systems 

Location: Mainly remote within the United States, with onsite collaboration in Laurel, Maryland, typically one day approximately every six weeks for team-wide sprint planning.

This position supports a pending contract opportunity and is contingent upon contract award, with an anticipated start in November 2026.

Build Applied AI for Secure Mission Software 

Help turn generative-AI concepts into dependable capabilities used within secure mission-planning and decision-support software.

At Rackner , you will integrate large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, agentic AI, prompt-engineering workflows, and inference pipelines into an established software application supporting a high-impact national-security mission. You will work across AI, software engineering, cybersecurity, DevSecOps, and customer technical teams to move capabilities beyond standalone demonstrations and into practical application workflows.

This role offers the opportunity to deepen your applied-AI experience, influence how emerging capabilities are designed and evaluated, and contribute to software where reliability, security, and mission usefulness matter.

- Evaluate AI outputs for grounding, reliability, accuracy, relevance, and mission usefulness.

- Participate in code reviews, technical reviews, and security-remediation activities.

What You Bring 

- A master’s degree or Ph.D. in Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Computer Science, or a related field, along with demonstrated experience working on or developing AI/ML capabilities.

- At least four years of relevant AI/ML experience that includes work with large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, and prompt engineering.

- Hands-on experience integrating LLM-enabled software and RAG capabilities into applications or workflows.

- Developing or supporting agentic-AI capabilities and multi-step AI workflows.

- Testing and documenting AI-enabled software capabilities.

- Secure software-development lifecycle and DevSecOps practices.

- OpenShift, Kubernetes, CI/CD, or containerized application delivery.

- Secure, restricted, disconnected, on-premises, or classified development environments.

- Defense, government, aerospace, mission-planning, or other regulated environments.

- Collaboration with software-engineering, cybersecurity, platform, and customer-facing technical teams.

Why Rackner 

At Rackner, you will have the opportunity to build technology that supports critical defense and public-sector missions.

You will work on more than isolated AI experiments or prompt-engineering tasks. This role combines hands-on LLM integration, retrieval and agentic-AI development, secure software delivery, and close collaboration across AI, software, cybersecurity, DevSecOps, and mission-focused teams.

Rackner has delivered more than $30 million in recent federal awards and supports mission-critical work across defense, civilian, and public-sector environments. Benefits & Professional Growth

We are seeking a talented and motivated, best-in-class Data Engineer II. This role presents an exciting opportunity to thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced environment within a rapidly growing team, with abundant prospects for career advancement. This position will own the data pipelines, transformations, and reporting processes that support accurate, complete, and timely furnishing of customer account information to credit bureaus.

This role presents an opportunity to work in a fast-paced, high growth environment while taking hands-on ownership of a critical customer-facing data function. You will dig into account data and code, debug SQL and Python workflows, and carry issues from investigation through verified resolution. You will partner with Customer Service to resolve technical dispute escalations, with Compliance to apply approved reporting requirements, and with Engineering when a fix is needed in production services or the consumer app. We are looking for an independent problem solver who can manage recurring reporting operations while improving the systems behind them.

- Trace discrepancies from account activity and source records through transformation logic to furnished outputs; identify root causes and implement lasting fixes

- Partner with Engineering on defects in production services or the consumer app, providing reproducible examples, affected-account analysis, and clear requirements; validate fixes through the reporting pipeline

- Document reporting logic, data lineage, procedures, and incident resolutions so the process is repeatable and can be supported by others
